events.event_narrative: Several utility poles were blown down.  A farm outbuilding had its roof torn off and sustained siding damage.
A shed was torn off its foundation and a swingset was twisted and demolished.  Multiple utility poles were blown down on N 2500 East Road.
Utility poles were blown down 1 to 2 miles west of Forrest.

A NWS damage survey confirmed a concentrated area of straight line winds with estimated peak winds of 80 mph occurred in and west of Forrest.  These strong winds blew off a portion of the roof of a junior high school gymnasium.  Numerous trees and utility poles were blown down.  At least one shed was damaged.
Multiple reports of street and yard flooding in Manteno were shared on social media.
A large tree limb was blown down onto North Mill Street.
Multiple large tree limbs were blown down on the east side of Cullom.  A video shared via broadcast media showed a brief burst of strong winds blowing tree debris around.

A tornado with peak winds of 90 mph touched down just south of 4H Park Road on the northwest side of Pontiac and immediately moved northeast across the Motorola and Vermillion Estates Subdivisions.  The tornado caused roofing and siding damage to a number of houses, apartments and manufactured homes.  Two houses had large portions of roofing blown off, leave the attics exposed.  The tornado crossed Route 23 and produced additional siding and fascia damage to a few manufactured homes in the Redwood mobile home park before ending north of E 1830 North Road.  The tornado also damaged several trees along its path.

A tornado with estimated peak winds of 80 mph touched down just southeast of the intersection of N 400 East Road and E 2900 North Road, west of Clifton.  Three utility poles were snapped as the tornado moved northeast across E 2900 North Road.  Roofing material was peeled off of a house and trees were damaged at the intersection of N 500 East Road and E 2900 North Road.  As the tornado crossed N 600 East Road and E 2950 North Road, two farm outbuildings had portions of their roofs ripped off at the same property. Additional tree damage was noted. The tornado lifted before reaching N 700 East Road.

A tornado with estimated peak winds of 85 mph touched down just southwest of the intersection of E 300 North Road and N 450 E Road.  The tornado crossed the intersection and peeled a west-facing section of metal roof eastward off an agricultural office building. While no condensation funnel was evident, eyewitnesses reported visible rotation in the clouds passing over the facility and debris from the impacted building getting lofted and swirled around in the air before being deposited in a field east of the facility where the tornado ended.  This was the only damage reported from this tornado.

A tornado with peak winds of 95 mph touched down in a field approximately two miles east of Clifton.  In the first few minutes of its lifespan, the tornado largely remained over open fields and may have briefly lifted as little damage was observed west of Route 45.  The tornado began to strengthen as it moved northeast and at the intersection of N 1600 East Road and E 3100 North Road, a sizable portion of an eastward facing roof of a house was torn off and deposited in a downstream field.  Several trees at this property were damaged including one pine tree whose top half was snapped off and tossed nearly 100 yards to the east.  At an adjacent property, a barn was shifted off of its foundation and had a portion of its roof peeled off.||As the tornado reached the Iroquois River, it tore the roof off of a garage and peeled roofing material off of a house at a property next to the river. Extensive tree damage was noted at this property and just to the east along the river, where multiple trees were uprooted and dozens of trees lost limbs.  The tornado weakened a bit east of the Iroquois River, but continued to cause tree damage as it approached and crossed N 1800 East Road.  A residence along N 1900 East Road and two additional barns along N 2000 East Road were damaged by the tornado.  The tornado lifted southwest of St. Anne, shortly after it tipped over an irrigation pivot.

A tornado with peak winds of 85 mph touched down just west of N 1300 East Road near Langan Creek, northeast of Clifton producing minor tree damage. Little to no damage was observed as the tornado moved across open farm fields on either side of Route 45.  The tornado peeled roof shingles off a house and damaged multiple farm outbuildings along N 1500 East Road, just north of E 3200 North Road.  A barn was blown off of its foundation, while a garage collapsed entirely.  The tornado lifted before reaching the Iroquois River as no damage was observed to the tree line along the river.

Storm spotters and chasers captured footage of a funnel cloud south of Martinton that lasted several minutes.  Photos and video showed that the funnel cloud was intermittently in contact with the ground as it moved northeast across open fields between N 1900 East Road and N 2400 East Road.  The last footage of the funnel cloud was captured around 15:59 CST as it dissipated east of Martinton, south of E 2800 North Road.  There was no known damage from this tornado.
A tree was blown down near the intersection of E 2880 North Road and N 3100 East Road.

Flooding occurred across many areas in northern and central Lake County.  In Crown Point, multiple areas were flooded due to clogged storm drains.  Flooding was reported near 97th Street and Buchanan Street and South Street near Court Street.  Near Hammond, a photo showed Broadmoor Avenue closed at Manor Avenue due to flooding.  East of Griffith, street flooding was reported near 47th Avenue and Hatcher Boulevard.  Near Gary, a photo showed 4th Avenue at Hamilton Street flooded. Water was also across sidewalks and low-lying sections of yards.  In Schererville, a photo showed flooding of yards and fields along Cline Avenue near a cemetery, where the side entrance to the cemetery was inundated.  In St. John, widespread flooding occurred.  Multiple roadways had flooded sections including at Tall Grass Trail and 93rd Avenue.  The retention pond at Prairie Pond Park overflowed into nearby park land.  Poor drainage areas were flooded along Parrish Avenue near 85th Avenue with ditches full and nearing the roadway.

Flooding was reported in many areas including many roads in central and southern Portage flooded with 6 to 12 inches of standing water.  Many ditches and retention ponds were full and overflowing.  Willowcreek Road was flooded with several inches of standing water and multiple vehicles were stuck in the flood waters.  A photo showed Crisman Ditch at bankfull with Stone Avenue culvert at capacity.
Lane flooding was reported on Interstate 94 one mile east of Chesterton.  A photo showed lanes flooded near the Route 49 interchange.
Nickel size hail was reported 1.9 miles northeast of Huntley.
Penny to nickel size hail lasting 10 minutes was reported in Cary.
Penny size hail was reported at Route 83 and North Avenue.
A tree was blown down onto a house near Warren Avenue and Warrenville Road.

events.event_narrative: Flooding was reported on numerous streets and roadways, including in Lemont, Homer Glen, Oak Lawn, Chicago Ridge and Hickory Hills.  In the City of Chicago, street flooding was reported in Washington Park and Auburn Gresham.  Basement flooding was reported in Chicago Lawn, Ashburn, West Englewood and Auburn Gresham.  Route 83 was flooded between Archer Avenue and Route 45.  Rainfall reports included 2.89 inches near Crestwood and 2.70 inches in Oak Lawn.

Flooding was reported on numerous streets and roadways across central Cook County including in the City of Chicago.  Street flooding was reported in Burbank, Uptown, Lincoln Square, Albany Park, Irving Park, Near West Side, Garfield Park, Downtown Chicago and in Hyde Park. Basement flooding was reported in Belmont Gragin, Austin, Humboldt Park, West Garfield Park, Garfield Ridge, Clearing, Archer Heights, West Elsdon, West Lawn, Dunning, Portage Park and Irving Park.||Specific reports of flooding included a public transportation bus stuck in floodwaters near 47th Street and Wood Street.  The California Avenue underpass at Interstate 55 was flooded and impassable.  Ashland Avenue viaducts were flooded between 15th Street and 16th Street.  The Route 34 underpass east of Route 45 was closed due to flooding.  A water rescue was reported at a flooded underpass on Kedzie Avenue between Interstate 55 and 31st Street.  Multiple lanes of Interstate 90 were flooded between North Avenue and Division Street.  A vehicle was stalled in flood waters at Carroll Avenue and Sacramento Boulevard.||Rainfall reports included 3.37 inches near La Grange; 2.27 inches in Burbank and 2.25 inches near Brighton Park.
Street flooding was reported in Naperville, Woodridge, Darien, Wheaton and Lombard.  Rainfall reports included 2.27 inches two miles southwest of Wheaton and 2.24 inches near Downers Grove.
Video shared on social media showed street flooding in multiple locations in Joliet.  Rainfall reports included 2.92 inches in Rockdale and 2.77 inches near Lockport.
Street flooding was reported in multiple areas in Wheeling, Prospect Heights and Mount Prospect.
Power lines were blown down at 3800 South Artesian Avenue.
A traffic light was blown down onto a moving car at the intersection of Cicero Avenue and 55th Street.  The car's windshield was cracked but no serious injuries were reported.
Numerous utility poles were blown down in the general area of Western Avenue and Fullerton Avenue.

Extensive wind damage occurred across southern parts of the City of Kankakee.  The damage began along West Jeffery Street and extended east of the Cobb Park area. About ten heating, ventilation and cooling units on the roof were either damaged or blown completely off the roof.  Damage was also reported inside the school. A tornado developed about one half mile east of Plainfield Naperville Road and about one block south of Boughton Road.  There was a narrow path of more intense damage in a subdivision where several homes had sections of roofing torn off, siding and soffits torn loose, trees snapped and limbs blown down.  The most intense damage was on Sparrow Lane, Maroon Bell Lane and Silverado Street.  The tornado was rated EF1 at this point.  Here one house was likely a total loss due to structural damage to the roof, covered porch, garage and one wall.  A garage was destroyed at another home.  The tornado weakened to EF0 east of this area from Kings Road to Indian Chase Meadows.  There was sporadic damage to trees and limbs and a few homes had damage to shingles, siding and soffits.  A small section of roof was removed from a house just east of Indian Chase Meadows.  At this point, the tornado appears to have dissipated, but strong straight line winds fanned out.

Strong straight line winds fanned out across a one quarter to one half mile wide path through Bolingbrook.  Damage began just south of Clow Airport.  Fences were blown down and sporadic minor tree damage continued.  In an older subdivision with larger more mature trees, there were numerous tree limbs blown down and a few trees snapped or uprooted.  But the houses were more sheltered by the larger trees and there was little damage to homes in this area.  The strong winds continued east of Veterans Parkway.  Small limbs were blown down at Jane Adams School.  From the school east southeast to Schmidt Road, a few homes had siding peeled back or soffits damaged.  There was sporadic damage to small trees and loose objects such as trampolines.  Portable basketball sets were blown over.  Winds were likely 60 to 75 mph in this area.  East of Schmidt Road, along Remington Road and Frontage Road, damage to tree limbs was very minor.  A construction trailer on Frontage Road, east of Woodcreek Drive was destroyed.  Winds were estimated to be 85 to 95 mph at this point.  South of Interstate 55, a large metal hotel sign was broken and a wooden pole holding a tornado siren was snapped.  There was damage to an air conditioning unit on the roof of an industrial building.  There was minor damage to trees along Old Chicago Road, east of Route 53 to Joliet Road.  Large trees were damaged on Joliet Road.  East along Bluff Road from Joliet Road to near Interstate 355, only sporadic minor damage to tree limbs was found with winds around 50 to 60 mph.  A softball backstop at the Remington Lakes Sports Complex was damaged extensively.

A brief tornado touched down in an industrial area near Fox Court.  It continued east northeast across South Gary Drive and dissipated near Stratford Square Mall.  A large warehouse had a wall blown out near Fox Court and Madsen Drive.

A second, brief tornado touched down in Bloomingdale, near an apartment complex on Century Point Lane.  There was roof and window damage at two apartment buildings.  Significant damage was done to roofs of houses and to trees from Cardinal Drive east across Bloomingdale Road through Norton Lane and into the area around Sterling Drive.
A tree fell onto a house along Army Trail Road.  One person was injured.
A large tree was blown down near Plainfield Naperville Road at 111st Street, blocking the road.
Apartment buildings suffered roof damage.  Two houses were damaged by fallen trees and one multi-family house had it's roof completely torn off.

A tornado touched down along the south side of 135th Street, one block east of LaGrange Road.  It moved southeast through the neighborhood along Howe Drive snapping off numerous tree tops, downing three or four large trees, blowing down a fence, sending a gazebo swirling 30 feet into the air before depositing it in a neighbor's yard and damaging a roof on an auto shop along Southwest Highway.  A car was also damaged by a falling tree limb.  At this point, the weakening tornado was wiped out by a microburst as it crossed the railroad trucks just east of Southwest Highway about a quarter mile south of 135th Street.

A microburst began near the railroad tracks just east of Southwest Highway about one quarter mile south of 135th Street.  The microburst widened, causing a damage path one quarter mile wide and about one third mile long.  The microburst blew down numerous trees in the area of Carolina Lane, 92nd Avenue, Elm Street, and 137th and 138th Streets.  Trees fell on rooftops, shingles were blown off a shed, there was damage to eaves of homes and there was porch and eave damage due to falling trees and tree limbs.  Power lines were also downed due to falling tree limbs.

A tornado touched down just northeast of the Ridge Road and Cline Avenue intersection.  Damage occurred at the Griffith Park Plaza Mall where windows were blown out of a row of stores and a portion of a roof was blown off of a vacant store.  The damage path continued to the east, behind the mall.  Two parked semi-trailers in the back of the mall were shifted eastward while a third was completely knocked over.  The area to the east of this mall in the subdivision along and north of 37th Avenue near Lafayette Avenue and Rensselaer Avenue sustained some of the strongest wind damage from this tornado.  Two houses on Lafayette Avenue had their roofs blown off with another house on Rensselaer Avenue also having its roof collapsed and a garage door pushed inward.  Other significant damage that occurred was at the Habitat for Humanity storage building at Colfax and Ridge Road.  Here, a cinder block storage building completely toppled to the ground.  Although the building was knocked over, it appears as though the main cause of it faltering was due to a large tree that fell on top of it.  At a nearby gas station within feet of this building, no damage occurred and people actually witnessed the tornado descend on the shelter.

Wind damage was evident beginning one mile south of Boswell near U.S. 41 and extending southeast along a fairly continous path for about 3 miles. Based on video evidence, a brief EF-0 tornado occurred just north of Pontiac. Surveillance video shared by a property owner showed a clear circulation with multiple sub-vortices on a quarry lake just west of 1600 East Road, north of old US-66. The tornado was observed in storm chaser videos crossing old US-66 just south of North Creek. Damage along the path of the tornado included the removal of a roof to a boat house and damage to a dock, garage, and fence. The maximum width of the tornado of 175 yards was estimated from the aforementioned surveillance and storm chaser videos. Peak winds were estimated at 75 mph.

A Livingston County deputy reported a brief tornado near 2200 North Road and old US-66 east of the community of Cayuga. The time and location of the report was consistent with rotation indicated by radar. There is no known damage that was caused by the tornado.

Two separate storm chaser videos showed a brief EF-U tornado occurring in a field near Kensington Avenue and S 1000W Road in Kankakee Township. Swirl patterns identified in a field from Gray Sky satellite imagery were used to approximate the start and end locations of the tornado. There is no known damage that was caused by the tornado.

Three separate storm chaser videos showed a brief EF-U tornado occurring in a field north of W 3500S Road and east of Illinois State Route 115. Swirl patterns noted in a field from Gray Sky satellite imagery were used to identify the start and end locations of the tornado. There is no known damage that was caused by the tornado.

An EF-1 tornado that was a satellite to the impactful Aroma Park area EF-3 tornado formed northeast of Aroma Park. High-resolution satellite imagery, storm chaser video, and radar data all depicted a generally southward-moving satellite tornado. Storm chaser video looking southeast from IL-17 captured the development of the tornado, which initially moved southwestward for about 30 seconds before becoming obscured by rain. Clear swirl marks (including several loops) were evident in a field north of S. Sandbar Road in Gray Sky satellite imagery near the start of the tornado. As the tornado continued southward, it uprooted a grove of trees in the vicinity of S. Sandbar Road, consistent with wind speeds near 90 mph. Sporadic tree damage was noted in high-resolution satellite imagery south of the Kankakee River, just to the east of a subdivision on Bittersweet Drive, before the tornado dissipated.

Video shared on social media taken on S 8250E Road approximately three quarters of a mile south of IL-17 showed a ground circulation occurring in a field to the west, coincident with a brief circulation noted in radar imagery. Swirl patterns were also identified in Gray Sky satellite imagery where the tornado was observed. There is no known damage that was caused by the tornado.

Video taken from S 13000E Road south of E 1000S Road looking west showed a brief anticyclonic tornado occurring in a field. Video time stamp and location matches an area of anticyclonic rotation seen on radar imagery. There is no known damage that was caused by the tornado.

An anticyclonic satellite tornado occurred north of Hopkins Park. High-resolution satellite imagery depicted swirl marks across multiple fields in the general vicinity of Baseline, S 13000E, and N 13500E Roads in a counter-clockwise looping path. Based on radar imagery and swirl patterns, the tornado appeared to be a anticyclonic tornado that initially moved north, stalled, and then turned southward before ending just north of a residence on S 13000 E Road, less than 300 yards southwest of the start location. There is no known damage that was caused by the tornado.

An EF-1 tornado with estimated peak winds of 110 mph tracked across northern Jasper County south of Stoutsburg, Wheatfield, and Dunns Bridge. This tornado began about 2 miles south of Stoutsburg along CR W 1000 N, where there was damage noted to a solar panel field and power poles. The tornado moved east-northeast, causing damage to a farmstead on CR N 200 W. The most significant damage from this tornado was noted just south of Wheatfield on the 0-100 block of CR W 1100 N and on the 1100 block of State Route 49, where numerous homes sustained considerable damage and numerous trees and power poles were downed. The tornado continued to damage solar panel fields, trees, power poles, and farmsteads as it moved toward the Starke County line, passing through the unincorporated community of Tefft. The tornado dissipated before reaching Starke County on the 500 block of CR E 1350 N. Three minor injuries were reported with the tornado.

As of this writing, the hailstone is being considered for the official Illinois state record.

A destructive EF-3 tornado with peak winds of 160 mph impacted portions of central and eastern Kankakee County before moving into northwest Indiana. The most notable damage caused by this tornado in Kankakee County occurred in the Aroma Park area. This tornado began just north of W 3000S Road southwest of Kankakee, IL, about one mile east of State Route 115. The tornado intensified while traveling east-northeastward into the far southern section of the city of Kankakee in the vicinity of Route 45, where concentrated higher end EF-1 tree damage and structural damage was observed. The tornado intensified further while moving across E 2500S Road, destroying a two-story home and several metal farm buildings, consistent with EF-3 caliber wind speeds. Concentrated extreme tree damage was noted, with numerous large hardwood trees snapped, stubbed, or uprooted despite lacking leaves, likely due to extensive debris lofting in the area.|After crossing I-57 and the Kankakee River, the tornado rapidly increased in size, producing a swath of significant damage in and near northern portions of Aroma Park. In this area, multiple homes were heavily damaged to an estimated EF-2 intensity. The tornado's peak width occurred here and was estimated to be approximately 1550 yards. Ground survey and aerial imagery suggests that the tornado further intensified as it tracked east-southeast before crossing the Kankakee River again. Within a narrow 150-200 yard wide section along S. Sandbar Road to the northeast of Aroma Park, three homes were completely destroyed, consistent with EF-3 caliber winds, and multiple others were heavily damaged and rendered uninhabitable. A heavy pickup truck parked in front of the garage of one of the destroyed homes was moved over 100 feet into a ditch next to the driveway, possibly being spun around the remnants of a small tree before reaching the ditch. In addition, on the other side of Sandbar Road, a crossover type SUV appeared to have been rolled onto the adjacent property and deposited onto a pile of debris just north of a heavily damaged residence. Along the swath of the most intense structural damage, concentrated extreme tree damage was noted, with numerous large hardwood trees snapped, stubbed, or uprooted despite lacking leaves, likely owing to extensive flying debris. Along Sandbar Road and through the Kankakee Elks Golf Course, the tornado's width was estimated at near 1500 yards. The tornado then continued generally east to east-northeast towards the Indiana state line, downing numerous additional trees, causing occasional structural damage, and flipping irrigation pivots as it moved just north of the communities of Wichert and Hopkins Park. The tornado continued on its destructive path into Newton County, Indiana where it caused additional EF-3 damage before eventually lifting west of De Motte in Jasper County. It was on the ground for over 35 miles and, at its peak, spanned a half mile in diameter. The storm destroyed numerous homes and resulted in around a dozen injuries and three fatalities: one in Aroma Park and the other two in Newton County, Indiana.

A destructive EF-3 tornado with estimated peak winds of 160 mph impacted portions of Newton and northwest Jasper Counties, most notably the community of Lake Village. After forming and causing EF-3 damage in Kankakee County, Illinois, this tornado crossed into Newton County between W 800 N Road and W 900 N Road near N 650 W Road. Upon entering the county, the tornado destroyed multiple outbuildings and significantly damaged multiple homes. On N 600 W Road, multiple homes were completely destroyed with debris blown clear of the foundations, consistent with EF-3 caliber winds. Nearby forested areas had almost all trees snapped or uprooted with some trees remaining standing with only stubs of a few large branches remaining, likely due to extensive lifted debris. Multiple homes were damaged, and a farm outbuilding was destroyed along N 500 W Road and along and near N 400 W Road. As the tornado crossed US-41 into the south side of Lake Village, it widened to approximately 1100 yards while damaging the roof and canopy of a gas station and a nearby retail building. Further north along N 300 W Road, multiple blocks of homes had significant roof damage and almost all trees were uprooted or snapped. The tornado continued eastward into a wooded area near the Lugene Links Golf Course, where a continuous corridor of trees was entirely uprooted. As the tornado neared W 950 N Road and N 150 W Road, a few homes were damaged, and a farm outbuilding was completely destroyed. The tornado continued to produce damage to trees and outbuildings as it traveled northeastward through mainly rural portions of northern Newton County and northern portions of Roselawn. The tornado continued into Jasper County and dissipated shortly thereafter. It was on the ground for over 35 miles and, at its peak, spanned a half mile in diameter. The storm destroyed numerous homes and resulted in around a dozen injuries and three fatalities: one in Kankakee County and the other two near Lake Village.

A destructive EF-3 tornado was nearing the end of its lifecycle upon briefly moving into northwest Jasper County and dissipated shortly thereafter. After forming in Kankakee County and causing EF-3 caliber damage in Kankakee and Newton counties, this tornado crossed into far northwestern Jasper County between W 1100 N Road and W 1200 N Road. Along N 1200 W Road just east of I-65, a continuous corridor of trees was entirely uprooted, a few outbuildings were damaged, and the roof was removed from a house. In the community of Forest City, a continuous corridor of trees was uprooted, and a few residences had shingles removed. The tornado diminished in intensity as it moved northeast toward N 1100 W Road, and then dissipated just south of the intersection of N 1100 W Road and W 1300 N Road. The tornado resulted in three fatalities and around a dozen injuries, though none reported in Jasper County. The damage sustained in Jasper County was found to be on the order of EF-1 strength.
Multiple reports of hail ranging in size from 1 inch in diameter to the size of golf balls came out of Lake Holiday and the south side of Somonauk. Time estimated using radar.
A few 1 inch hail reports came out of the Plano and Millbrook areas. Time estimated using radar.
A public report was received of roofing and siding damage, solar panels peeled back from a roof, and 12 inch diameter trees snapped northeast of Pecatonica. Time estimated using radar.
Street, yard and basement flooding was reported in Dolton. A long stretch of 144th Street near Indiana Avenue was flooded.
Multiple county roads were flooded near N 400 E Road south of Flanagan with multiple cars stuck in flood waters.
A vehicle was reported stuck in flood waters on the exit ramp from Interstate 55 to Route 47.
Standing flood waters 4 to 6 inches deep was reported at the Interstate 55 underpass to Joliet Road.

Several videos were shared of a slow-moving landspout tornado that occurred a few miles east of Beaverville and north northeast of Donovan in rural northeast Iroquois County. No known damage was reported.
A large recreational vehicle was destroyed when half of a large tree fell on it near the intersection of Freeport and Milledgeville Roads.
A large tree limb fell onto a parked car.  Power lines were also blown down.

A large tree was blown down into a parking lot at the corner of South Fourth Street and Grove Street.  Another tree was blown down blocking 10th Street just south of East Lincoln Highway.  Numerous tree limbs and power lines were also blown down.
Trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down in Berwyn.  Some of the tree limbs fell onto cars.

Part of the roof of the Manhattan Township Building was peeled back by strong winds.  Rain fell through the openings, putting weight on the drywall ceilings, which eventually fell onto township equipment and the Manhattan Food Pantry located on the top level of the building.  Much of the damage was caused by the rain.

A police car and a second car, parked next to each other near Route 26 and Haldane Road, were damaged when a tree fell onto them.  Many trees were damaged in Haldane and a large antenna was blown down along Route 26.
Ten to twelve trees on the north side of Wheaton were damaged.  Power lines were also blown down.
Numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down across Earlville.  Wind damage was also reported to fences and store signs.
A house was struck by lightning on Prairie Street, sparking a fire in the kitchen.  Damage was limited to the stove, a wall, cabinet and a window.
A 100 foot tall maple tree fell onto a house on Prairie Street.  The tree broke a window and pulled off parts of a gutter.
Sheet metal and insulation were torn off a soap factory by strong winds.  Most of the damage was cosmetic, no structual damage was reported.
A barn was completely blown off its foundation north of Oregon.  A cattle trailer was lifted airborne before landing upside down.  At least 50 trees suffered significant wind damage.
A house on East Hawthorne Boulevard was struck by lightning, which caused a fire in the attic.  The house suffered roof and ceiling damage.
Lightning struck a tree on N. Ridgeland Avenue, then jumped to electrical wires and into a house.  Several electrical appliances were destroyed and a fire was started in the basement.
Lightning struck a house on Dunoulin Avenue causing a fire and moderate to heavy damage.
The roof of a storage building collapsed on Mondamin Street.

An NWS damage survey confirmed that an EF-1 tornado with estimated peak winds of 100 mph began in far northeastern Whiteside County west of Palmyra before moving northeast into Lee County. It tracked for over 6.5 miles before lifting near the town of Woosung. The tornado damaged or destroyed multiple farm outbuildings, downed several trees and power poles, and caused minor damage to a few residences.

An NWS damage survey confirmed that a brief EF-1 tornado with estimated peak winds of 105 mph impacted a few properties along Ridge Road in southern Ogle County. One house had two-thirds of its roof removed by the tornado and several trees were damaged by the tornado as well.

An NWS damage survey confirmed that an EF-0 tornado with estimated peak winds of 85 mph tracked through the community of Holcomb in northeastern Ogle County. The tornado caused extensive tree damage in Holcomb, damaged a few farm outbuildings, and caused a grain leg to collapse onto railroad tracks.
An emergency manager estimated 60 to 70 mph thunderstorm winds in Dixon.
A trained spotter reported 2 inch tree limbs downed by thunderstorm winds in Oregon.
An NWS employee reported roofing or other structural material on the road, as well as a downed tree at a farm just east of I-39.
Broadcast media reported a tree down on a house on the 600 block of S Jefferson St in Woodstock.
A report of siding damage, the partial loss of a tree, and other various objects blown around came out of Woodstock.
A large tree was down and blocking IL-120 between Wonder Lake Dr and Thompson Rd. Seven power poles were also downed in the same area.
A photo was shared of a tree down across Columbus St just north of E Jackson St in Ottawa.
A tree was downed along McCullom Lake Rd east of Wonder Lake.
A tree was uprooted and a metal sign blown over west of Pistakee Highlands.
Multiple reports were received of trees downed on the north side of Antioch.
Multiple reports were received of trees and tree branches down at and near Sunset Knoll Park in Lombard.
An 8 inch tree branch was downed near Winfield.
Multiple large tree branches were downed in and near Garfield Park. A small tree was also uprooted.
Multiple large tree branches and limbs were downed in and around the Garfield Park community area of Chicago.

Thunderstorm wind gusts were estimated at 60 mph at the NWS Chicago WFO.
Power poles were downed north of Manhattan.

events.event_narrative: Thunderstorm wind gusts peaked at 66 mph at the Michigan City C-MAN station.
A photo was shared of a tree uprooted in Durand.
A tree was downed along Poplar Grove Rd south of Poplar Grove.
Power lines were downed on the north side of Hampshire.
A tree was down on Chicago St in Elgin.
A wire was down at IL-47 and Burlington Rd north of Lily Lake.

events.event_narrative: Standing water was reported along Auburn St east of Auburn High School in Rockford.
A few inches of standing water on the road were reported near Island Lake.
A few inches of standing water on the road were reported on the west side of Waukegan.
A few inches of standing water on the road were reported north of Gurnee and west of Zion.
A few inches of standing water on the road were reported in Winthrop Harbor.
A few inches of standing water on the road were reported south of Antioch.
A heavy thunderstorm produced a funnel cloud over Ogle County as it tracked from south of Oregon northeast toward Davis Junction.

An NWS storm survey found a corridor of wind damage near and southeast of Seward. Siding and roofing damage was found on a couple of farm outbuildings, two power poles were downed north of Seward, and multiple large trees and branches were downed.
Emergency management reported a tree down northeast of Byron.
At least one basement was flooded in Machesney Park.
A semitruck was overturned on I-88 westbound near Dauberman Rd causing westbound lanes to be shut down.
Power lines and possibly some power poles were downed along Dauberman Rd south of Kaneville.
Trees were reported down and blocking the road at Keslinger and Harley Roads near La Fox.

events.event_narrative: An EF-1 tornado with peak winds around 90 mph dropped in rural northeast McLean County before crossing into Livingston County southwest of Fairbury. In the few minutes the tornado survived in Livingston County, it damaged trees and a machine shed.
Storm chaser video showed a brief tornado touched down in an open field three miles from north of Pecatonica. The tornado was only on the ground for about two minutes and caused no known damage.

A high-end EF-1 tornado began near Meridian Road between Favor Road and Steward Road southeast of Harrison, initially causing damage to trees and an outbuilding. Video footage from storm chasers documented the tornado becoming fully condensed and growing in size and intensity as it tracked east-northeastward across Favor Road and impacted two farmsteads, causing significant damage to a few outbuildings and snapping and uprooting multiple trees. Additional storm chaser footage showed the tornado intensifying again as it tracked northeastward across Gummow Road and then reaching peak intensity as it impacted a property along Freeport Road. At this property, the majority of an older two-story house's roof was removed, several trees were snapped, and an old barn was destroyed. The footage then captured the tornado making a sharp turn to the southeast and crossing Freeport Road once again before roping out and eventually dissipating in open fields near Owen Center Road.

An EF-1 tornado began near the intersection of Freeport Road and Bates Road southeast of Harrison, initially downing several tree branches at and near a small cemetery. The tornado produced additional tree damage as it tracked eastward along Roscoe Road before entering the west side of Roscoe and reaching its peak intensity as it tracked through the Hawks Point, Crystal Hills, and Oxford Commons subdivisions. There, multiple homes had portions of their roofs torn off or damaged and had sections of siding and fascia peeled off. A few homes also had their garage doors blown in, leading to parts of their garage walls getting blown out in a few cases. Numerous trees were also uprooted or damaged in these subdivisions. The tornado then continued eastward, knocking down several power poles along Gleasman Road and damaging a nearby farm outbuilding before crossing the Rock River. East of the Rock River, the tornado continued to cause extensive tree damage. Multiple additional houses sustained roof and fascia damage from the tornado as well. The tornado appeared to dissipate just as it reached the Winnebago-Boone County line. Extensive straight-line wind damage was also observed in close proximity to the tornadic circulation, particularly along its southern flank.

An EF-1 tornado with peak winds near 95 mph appeared to have started just south of County Road 2200 N in Bureau County, where a barn structure sustained roofing damage. The tornado then moved northeastward into LaSalle County, producing damage to trees and farm outbuildings. Several wooden power poles were damaged just southeast of Mendota before a semi truck was blown over on I-39 as the tornado continued northeastward. The tornado then passed near Meriden, causing additional damage to trees and farm outbuildings before dissipating in an open field northwest of Earlville.

An EF-1 tornado touched down on the west side of Gibson City, producing significant roofing damage to several buildings along 8th Street. The tornado continued ENE for several miles, producing primarily tree damage before lifting approximately three miles ENE of Gibson City.
A brief EF-0 tornado caused damage to trees and outbuildings near and northeast of Woodland.

An EF-1 tornado with peak winds near 95 mph touched down west of Loda with initial damage consisting of the collapse of two empty grain bins. The tornado continued ENE crossing into Iroquois County southwest of Buckley, downing and uprooting trees and blowing over semi-trucks on Interstate 57. Near the end of the damage track, the roof of a large outbuilding was removed, while nearby trees were snapped near the base and deposited in various directions.

An EF-1 tornado with peak winds near 95 mph touched down west of Loda with initial damage consisting of the collapse of two empty grain bins. The tornado continued ENE crossing into Iroquois County southwest of Buckley, downing and uprooting trees and blowing over semi-trucks on Interstate 57. Near the end of the damage track, the roof of a large outbuilding was removed, while nearby trees were snapped near the base and deposited in various directions.

An EF-1 tornado appeared to touch down in an open field southwest of the intersection of E 1200 North Road and N 2450 East Road and impacted a farm, leading to damage to several structures. The tornado then continued northeastward, causing damage to trees and farm outbuildings. The peak intensity of the tornado occurred near the end of the path along the Iroquois and Newton County border, where over a dozen new wooden power poles were snapped at their base. The tornado then appeared to lift just northeast of US-24 in southwestern Newton County.

An EF-1 tornado appeared to touch down in an open field southwest of Darrow in rural Iroquois County. It tracked northeast causing damage to trees and farm outbuildings. The peak intensity of the tornado occurred near the end of the path along the Iroquois and Newton County border, where over a dozen new wooden power poles were snapped at their base. The tornado then appeared to lift just northeast of US-24 in southwestern Newton County.

A brief EF-0 tornado started near Farr Creek in the small community of Eldridge within unincorporated Momence. Along the path, a combination of scattered tree damage and outbuilding roof damage was noted. As the tornado tracked north of the center of Momence, multiple power poles were downed along IL-1, with additional tree damage noted near 5500N. The tornado appears to have dissipated just northeast of Trimm Creek.

A narrow EF-1 tornado touched down near the intersection of W 1700 S and S 350 W roads near Kentland, where several large tree branches were downed. The tornado then crossed US Highway 41 at peak intensity, downing a billboard, uplifting a large portion of the roof of a restaurant, and pushing over a semi truck. A farm outbuilding was damaged nearby, as well. Debris was thrown nearly 2 miles downstream in an open field just north of US Highway 24. A narrow path evident in satellite imagery in open fields to the northeast of this debris suggested that the tornado likely continued to the northeast for approximately two more miles without impacting any trees or structures before dissipating.

This tornado began just west of the Illinois-Indiana state line near CR 9000N in northeast Kankakee County. The first instances of damage included uprooted softwood trees, downed large branches from hardwood trees, and minor structural damage noted near Stateline Rd on either side of the border. The storm continued northeast into Lake County, Indiana where it caused additional damage to trees and a handful of structures.

This tornado began just west of the Illinois-Indiana state line near CR 9000N in northeast Kankakee County. The first instances of damage included uprooted softwood trees, downed large branches from hardwood trees, and minor structural damage noted near Stateline Rd on either side of the border. As the tornado quickly tracked northeast, it caused additional tree damage on at least one property near US-41. Along the path toward and through Lowell, the tornado blew out sections of a gas station canopy along IN-2 and then a garage wall at a residence just northwest of downtown Lowell. This was in addition to causing further tree and minor structural damage in a defined narrow path. The tornado  continued through southern and southeastern sections of Lake Dalecarlia, causing primarily tree damage and minor structural damage due to fallen trees. Based on the ground survey, the tornado likely dissipated prior to reaching IN-55.
A few hail reports came from south of Durand ranging in size from 1.25 to 2.25 inches in diameter.
Several photos were received of broken windows and damaged siding from in and around Durand due to a combination of severe winds and hail.
Softwood trees were snapped near the intersection of Task Bridge Rd and Best Rd north of Pecatonica.
McHenry County emergency management reported a funnel cloud near Capron.
Photos shared via social media showed doors blown out of a farm outbuilding near Earlville.
Metal roofing was damaged on a building north of Leland.
A two foot diameter tree was down and blocking the southbound lane of Somonauk Rd just north of Pratt Rd in Sandwich.
Power lines were downed causing a tree to catch fire at IL-38 and Kirk Rd in Geneva.
Three power poles were blown over (not snapped) west of Cornell.
Several power lines were downed along IL-17 west of I-55 near Dwight.
A tree roughly two feet in diameter was snapped in Rolling Meadows.
An eight inch diameter tree limb was broken near the intersection of Oak St and American St in Paxton.

Emergency management reported extensive tree damage around Watseka, particularly the southeast part of town. Numerous uprooted trees and snapped trunks were reported. Two separate personal weather stations on the south and southeast sides of town recorded a 72 mph and a 73 mph gust.
Photos shared via social media showed downed power poles and trees in Bonfield.
Tree damage was reported around Manteno.
Extensive tree damage was noted around Kankakee, including downed branches up to one foot in diameter.
Photos shared showed snapped softwood trees and damaged fences in Momence.
Power poles and trees were downed in Beecher. A fire was started when one branch fell onto a power line.

events.event_narrative: Power poles were damaged in a number of spots near and north of Stoutsburg.
A fence was damaged and a large playground set rolled out of a yard in Wheatfield.
Numerous trees and power poles were downed around Lowell outside of the path of the EF-0 tornado.
Numerous tree branches were downed around and southwest of St. John.
Numerous power lines and poles were downed south of CR 1300S extending from State Line Rd to US-41.
A one foot diameter hardwood tree was uprooted near Lakes of the Four Seasons.

events.event_narrative: Standing water was reported on IL-173 near Oak Grove Rd in Alden.
Multiple reports were received of around six inches of standing water across IL-23 south of Harvard.
Flooding was reported along Rollins Rd in Fox Lake.
Flooding was reported at US-45 and Washington St in Third Lake.
Flooding was reported at US-41 and Buckley Rd in North Chicago.
The gauge on Buffalo Creek at Wheeling quickly rose to minor flood stage amid heavy rain and thunderstorms.
The gauge on the north branch of the Chicago River at Deerfield quickly rose to minor flood stage amid heavy rain and thunderstorms.
A fence was blown down in Northlake with gusts estimated at around 60 mph.

Large branches were broken and fell onto power lines in Sandwich. The upper portion of a large tree was broken and landed on a house north of Sandwich. Nearby personal weather stations recorded gusts to between 60 and 70 mph at the time.
Several reports of downed trees and large tree limbs were received from near and west of Aurora, including near the Aurora Airport which whose ASOS recorded a 67 mph peak gust.
Siding was removed from a house in Elgin.
An electrical transmission tower was leaning and seemingly being held up by the power lines.

Numerous reports of downed trees and tree limbs came out of central and east-central DuPage County, namely along a corridor extending from Wheaton to Villa Park. At least one large tree was uprooted in Villa Park.
Power lines were downed and a tree was downed onto a house southwest of Lake Barrington.
A 24 inch diameter tree snapped in Libertyville.

Multiple reports of downed power poles and trees, including some snapped at the base, came out of the vicinity of St. John, Cedar Lake, and Crown Point. Southeast of Schererville, a few trees were downed onto homes. One vehicle was struck by a falling power pole in St. John.
Multiple large branches and at least one tree were downed near Portage.
A 95-foot tall radio tower collapsed near Lincolnway and Yellowstone roads in Valparaiso. Large tree limbs were also reported down nearby.
A personal weather station recorded 2.4 inches of storm total rainfall east of Oxford through 7:15 PM EST, 2.36 of which fell between 6:00 and 7:15 PM.
A personal weather station recorded 2.31 inches of rainfall in Rockford between 6:00 and 7:00 PM CST.
A personal weather station recorded 1.81 inches of rainfall near Timberlane between 6:00 and 7:00 PM CST.
A tree was downed onto a truck in Buckley.
An eight to ten inch diameter tree limb was downed on E Patton St between Washington and College streets in Paxton.
A large tree was downed and blocking a driveway along IL-9 southeast of Elliot.
About half a dozen streets in Paxton were under three to four inches of water.

Widespread flash flooding occurred across parts of northern Cook County where numerous vehicles were disabled in flood waters including in Hoffman Estates, Hanover Park and Medinah.  At least two vehicles were stuck in flood waters on Weathersfield Way near Schaumburg.  A vehicle was disabled in flood waters on Busse Road under the Interstate 90 bridge.  Four cars were stuck in flood waters at the intersection of Roselle Road and Wise Road.  Street and viaduct flooding was reported in Des Plaines and Mount Prospect.  At least one basement flooded in Schaumburg and at least two basements flooded in Mount Prospect.  Rainfall amounts included 2.63 inches in Mount Prospect; 2.62 inches two miles east of Schaumburg and 2.10 inches in Elk Grove Village.

Widespread street and basement flooding was reported across much of northern Chicago, including Edison Park, Norwood Park, Jefferson Park, Rogers Park, Edgewater, Uptown, Forest Glen, North Park and West Ridge. Lakeshore Drive was flooded near Montrose Beach. The underpass on Interstate 94 at Pratt Avenue in Lincolnwood was flooded. In Edison Park, cars were reported stalled with water up to their bumpers.  Multiple roads and viaducts were flooded in Rosemont and near O'Hare Airport, including along portions of Interstate 90.  Rainfall amounts included 3.46 inches in Harwood Heights; 2.66 inches in Rogers Park; 2.59 inches in Park Ridge and 2.56 inches in Lincolnwood. Chicago O'Hare Airport measured 2.43 inches, which was a record 24 hour total for April 14th.

Hundreds of tree limbs were blown down across Homewood.  Most of the damage occurred on the northeast side of Homewood, particularly along Ridge Road between Riegel Road and Halsted Street.  Two Japanese elm trees were blown down onto a fence, just missing a house.  Another tree was blown down on two vehicles.
As many as 50 large tree limbs were blown down along with power lines in Oak Park.  A couple entire trees were also blown down.
A large tree was blown down onto a car, crushing the roof of the car.
A garage and part of a house along Wisconsin Street were ripped apart by strong winds.
Numerous tree limbs were blown down.  Part of a utility pole was blown down along with some power lines.
Several trees were blown down near Van Buren Avenue and 30th Street.  One tree fell onto a car.
Several tree limbs were blown down in Rensselaer including one large limb near Cherry and Melville Streets.
Trees and tree limbs were blown down.  A shed was knocked off of its foundation.
Several tree limbs and power lines were blown down.
Trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down between Dwight and Campus.
Trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down in Ottawa.

A tornado touched down approximately 5 miles northwest of Wheatfield near the Oak Heritage Estates.  This tornado caused structual damage to one mobile home, damage to multiple trees and corn fields.  Damage began southwest of the intersection of North 450 West and Hawthorn Road, where a 10 yard wide path of corn stalks was completely flattened in a convergent manner.  Damage continued where a roof was lifted off a mobile home and thrown into the yard.  Also at this location, two trees were completely uprooted.  Along the path of this tornado, the tops of many trees had sheared limbs along with scattered debris ranging from toys to trash bins.
Road 375E was closed north of Route 17 due to flooding.  Bloomington Road in South Streator was closed due to flooding.

Flash flooding began during the predawn hours and continued into the early afternoon hours across many locations in Kane County.  In Geneva, basement flooding was reported in the Emergency Operations Center, and the intersection of Route 25 and Fabyan Parkway was closed.  Near Elburn, Empire Road was flooded east of Hampton Road, the intersection of Route 64 and Route 47 was flooded under the train tracks.  Residential flooding was reported in Lily Lake.  In Elgin, numerous roads and intersections were closed including, Randall and Big Timber Roads, Canyon and Valley Creek, Mark and Mildred Roads, and Jewett and Orange Streets.  Flooding was also reported along Beckman Trail, the 300 block of Wilcox, the 400 block of Commonwealth and the 100 block of Brookside.  Between Elburn and Maple Park, Keslinger and Schneider Roads were flooded.  In Blackberry township, Main and Bunker Streets were flooded.  Blackberry Creek overflowed its banks in Aurora.  Storm total rainfall from early morning through early afternoon included 7.90 inches 7 miles northwest of St. Charles, 6.33 inches in St. Charles and 4.87 inches in Batavia.

Flash flooding was reported across many areas of Dupage County.  Street and yard flooding was reported near Wheaton.  A retention pond overflowed on Bartlett Road in Bartlett.  Major street and parking lot flooding was reported around Route 53 and North Avenue in Lombard.  Route 53 was closed south of Butterfield Road and North of Morton Arboretum because the east branch of the Dupage River had overflowed its banks.  A dam at the end of Lake Ellyn in Glen Ellyn overflowed and flooded numerous streets.  Rainfall totals included 6.40 inches in Carol Stream, 5.69 inches two miles north of Wheaton.

Flooding was reported at the following locations, First Avenue west of Berwyn; Palatine Road in Wheeling; North Avenue at Interstate 290 in Elmhurst; Interstate 90 near O'Hare Airport; Touhy Avenue near Mt. Prospect was impassible; Interstate 94 at Pratt, and along Weller Creek at Elmhurst Road.  Wilke Road between Kirchoff and Central was flooded in Arlington Heights.  Several feet of water was reported covering some taxiways and gate areas at O'Hare Airport.  Standing water was reported in streets and in fields in Evanston.  Park Boulevard was under water with a stalled car near Streamwood, and Popular Creek flooded fields.  In Northbrook, an overflowing stream flooded Green Park.  There were close to 200 reports of basement flooding in Chicago, along with a few flooded viaducts.  Over 5,000 residences in unincorporated Maine Township were affected by flooding and 86 basements were completely filled to the first floor with flood water.  Numerous vehicles were stuck or abandoned in flood waters including two police cars and an ambulance.  Flooding was also reported in Schaumburg, Palatine and Arlington Heights.  A 28 year old man attempted to swim across a flooded retention basin near the Sunset Meadows Park in Arlington Heights.  He was seen struggling in the water and rescue crews pulled his body out of the pond a few hours later.  A 13 year old boy was swept into Salt Creek in Elk Grove Village while crossing a foot bridge.  He was quickly rescued by onlookers.  A business in Rolling Meadows suffered significant flooding from two nearby retention ponds.  The Metropolitan Water Reclamation District reversed the flow of the Chicago River, sending mainly rainwater runoff into Lake Michigan at rate of 25 billion gallons per hour.  Rainfall totals included, 7.07 inches near Evanston, 6.60 inches near Elk Grove Village, 6.10 inches in Morton Grove and 5.89 inches in Streamwood.

Governors Highway in Matteson was closed early Saturday morning due to flooding.  In Tinley Park, the intersection of 88th and 175th was flooded.  A retention pond overflowed and sandbags were used to prevent flooding to nearby homes.  Other roads in Tinley Park were reported to have 3 to 6 inches of water.  Major flooding was reported in the Heather Hill Neighborhood in Flossmoor.  Rainfall of 4.50 inches was reported in Tinley Park.  The intersection of Sibley and Halsted in Harvey was flooded.
Flooding along Green River was reported in Amboy.  Rainfall in Amboy was approximately 6.50 inches.

Several streets were flooded in Mendota with three feet of water reported on 1st Street.  The Fourth Avenue viaduct south of Doenier Field was flooded.  Water was seen coming up through sewers.  Creeks also overflowed their banks.

Basement and street flooding was reported in Valparaiso.  Water was waist high in some locations with some roads impassible.  Street flooding was also reported in South Haven.  Route 2 near the Lake County Line was flooded and closed.
Basement flooding was reported in Highland.  Street flooding with 2 to 8 inches of water was reported on Glenwood, Laporte, Grand and Duluth Roads.
Interstate 94 was closed from Chesterton to the Porter-Laporte county line due to flooding.
Fields were reported flooded from 109th to 132nd Street and creeks had overflowed their banks.

After heavy rain and flash flooding across much of Kane County from the early morning through the afternoon of September 13th, flooding continued across many locations through the evening hours and into the early morning hours of September 14th, when another wave of heavy rain moved across the area.

After heavy rain and flash flooding across much of Dupage County from the early morning through the afternoon of September 13th, flooding continued across many locations through the evening hours and into the early morning hours of September 14th, when another wave of heavy rain moved across the area.

After heavy rain and flash flooding across much of northern and central Cook County from the early morning through the afternoon of September 13th, flooding continued across many locations through the evening hours and into the early morning hours of September 14th, when another wave of heavy rain moved across the area.

In Oswego, Route 25 was flooded and closed between Oswego and Montgomery Roads.  Several cars drove around the barricades and at least one car was swept into the Fox River.  The driver was able to escape.  Four miles south of Little Rock, Jetter Road was flooded and closed.  Three occupants of a car were rescued after their car was swept into Big Rock Creek.  In Plano, many roads were flooded and closed, including Hale Road, Main Street, Miller Road and Creek Road.  Extensive flooding was reported along Rock Creek Road.  The Farnsworth House in Plano was damaged by flood waters from the Fox River.  Extensive flooding was reported in Millington.  Part of Fox River Drive was washed away and 17 roads across Kendall County were closed due to flooding.  Basement flooding was also reported.

Flash flooding or significant flooding was reported across most of Dupage County, including street closures due to flooding, basement flooding and creek, stream and river flooding.  A few of the more extensive flooding reports included the West Branch of the Dupage River in and near Warrenville, in Addison where 1,800 people had to be evacuated, along Salt Creek in Villa Park and 300 houses were affected by flooding in Carol Stream.  Numerous vehicles were also reported stalled or abandoned in flood waters.

Flash flooding or significant flooding was reported across most of Cook County, including street closures due to flooding, basement flooding and creek, stream and river flooding.  In the Albany Park neighborhood in Chicago, the North Branch of the Chicago River overflowed its banks and flooded about 340 homes.  In Skokie, five people were rescued from three vehicles trapped in flood waters at the Golf Road viaduct and eight people were rescued from five vehicles stalled out under the Skokie Boulevard viaduct.  Silver Creek flooded streets and basements near Hillside.  Significant flooding was reported in Des Plaines including multiple vehicles submerged or abandoned.  Significant flooding was also reported in Park Ridge where at least 8 people had to be rescued from their vehicles which were stuck in flood waters.  Dozens of vehicles were abandoned in flood waters.  The basement of Riverside-Brookfield High School suffered major flood damage and the school was closed for one week.  Brookfield Zoo closed for the first time because so many exhibits were flooded.  Full moats in some exhibits would have allowed large carnivores to swim out, so they were forced to stay in their indoor habitats.  Significant flooding was reported in the Golf neighborhood of Glenview.
In Orland Hills, 167th Street was closed due to flooding between 88th Avenue and 94th Avenue.

Flash flooding or significant flooding was reported across most of Kane County, including street closures due to flooding, basement flooding and creek, stream and river flooding.  A few of the more extensive flooding reports included a wall of a retention pond that was washed away in South Elgin, flooding along the Fox River in Batavia, eight cars were pulled out of flood waters along Route 56 and in residential areas in Elgin near Popular Creek.  Numerous other vehicles were abandoned in flood waters.

Flash flooding or significant flooding was reported across much of DeKalb County, including street closures due to flooding, basement flooding and creek, stream and river flooding.  Extensive flooding was reported in the Evergreen mobile home park near Sycamore.  Street flooding was reported in Waterman, Hinckley and Shabbona.

Flash flooding or significant flooding was reported across most of Grundy County, including street closures due to flooding, basement flooding and creek, stream and river flooding.  Significant flooding was reported in Coal City.

Flash flooding or significant flooding was reported across much of LaSalle County, including street closures due to flooding, basement flooding and creek, stream and river flooding.  Numerous houses were under water in the northwest and southwest part of Sheridan which is near the Fox River.  Several evacuations were conducted.  Northeast of Utica, County Roads E 10th and and N 31st were closed with up to one foot of water covering the roads.  A canoe launch area in Streator along the Vermillion River was submerged.  Flooding was reported in Wedron, Utica, Earlville and Marseilles.  The wastewater treatment plant in the City of LaSalle suffered significant damage.  Numerous vehicles were submerged or abandoned in flood waters.

Numerous streets and viaducts were flooded in Bradley. There was 2 feet of water at Euclid and Erie.  Several streets and intersections were flooded and closed in Kankakee including Hobbie Avenue at Route 50 with 2 to 3 feet of water, and the Brookmont Boulevard viaduct with 1 to 2 feet of water.

Flash flooding or significant flooding was reported across most of western Will County, including street closures due to flooding, basement flooding and creek, stream and river flooding.  Extensive flooding was reported at Royce Road which was closed just west of Route 53 due to flooding from the East Branch of the Dupage River.  Weber Road was closed between Royce Road and Boughton Roads due to extensive flooding from the Dupage River.  Many roads were closed due to flooding in the southern part of Naperville.  Flooding was reported along the Dupage River in Plainfield.  Two vehicles were submerged along Plainfield Naperville Road in Plainfield.

Flash flooding or significant flooding was reported across many parts of eastern and central Will County, including street closures due to flooding, basement flooding and creek, stream and river flooding.  North Peotone Road had 8 to 12 inches of water just west of Harlem Avenue.

In Milford, the Route 1 viaduct was flooded and closed.  In Cissna Park, widespread flooding was reported with numerous flooded and closed roads.  Some people were evacuated from their homes.  Significant flooding was also reported in Watseka.
Widespread flooding across parts of Cook County slowly receded through September 16th.
Widespread flooding across parts of Cook County slowly receded through September 16th.
Widespread flooding across parts of Dupage County slowly receded through September 17th.
Widespread flooding across parts of Kane County slowly receded through September 17th.
Widespread flooding across parts of DeKalb County slowly receded through September 17th.

Widespread flooding across parts of La Salle County slowly receded through September 17th.  Five teenagers were injured on the evening of September 14th when the driver of the vehicle they were in, lost control on a water covered road.  The car entered a ditch and flipped over.
Widespread flooding across parts of Kendall County slowly receded through September 16th.
Widespread flooding across parts of Grundy County slowly receded through September 17th.
Widespread flooding across parts of Will County slowly receded through September 16th.
Widespread flooding across parts of Will County slowly receded through September 16th.
Widespread flooding across parts of Kankakee County slowly receded through September 16th.
Widespread flooding across parts of Iroquois County slowly receded through September 16th.

Flash flooding or significant flooding was reported across most of Lake County, including street closures due to flooding, basement flooding and creek, stream and river flooding.  Interstate 80/94 was closed due to flooding between Cline and Calumet Avenues.  Parts of Interstate 65 were closed due to flooding.  In Lake Station, 300 to 400 homes were evacuated.  In Merrillivlle, part of 73rd Avenue was washed away, where three cars were damaged.  In Dyer, Hart Ditch overtopped its banks which flooded the Briar Ridge Subdivision.  Flood waters were several feet deep in parts of Hobart after flood waters overflowed Lake George.  Numerous vehicles were submerged or abandoned.

Flash flooding or significant flooding was reported across most of Porter County, including street closures due to flooding, basement flooding and creek, stream and river flooding.  Two men were sucked into a culvert while trying to rescue a boy in flood waters in Chesterton.  The boy survived but both men drowned.  A sinkhole developed and swallowed the back of a fire truck in Valparaiso.
Widespread flooding across parts of Lake County slowly receded through September 17th.
Widespread flooding across parts of Porter County slowly receded through September 17th.
Roads were closed in Algonquin because Woods Creek overflowed.  Flooding was also reported in Lake in The Hills.

Flash flooding or significant flooding was reported across parts of Jasper County, including street closures due to flooding, basement flooding and creek, stream and river flooding.  Columbia Park was flooded in Rensselaer.  Flood waters surrounded homes and bussinesses in DeMotte.
Widespread flooding across parts of Jasper County slowly receded through September 16th.

Heavy rain caused significant flooding across parts of southern and central DeKalb County.  Stormtotal rainfall of 5.40 inches was reported in DeKalb.  Street flooding was reported in Hinckley and Waterman.

Flooding continued across parts of southern and central DeKalb County into the morning of September 14th.  A car drove into flood waters on Rimsnider Road near Hinckley during the evening of September 13th.  The car was swept away by fast flowing flood waters.  A man, woman and small child (along with their pets) in the car, were able to get out of the car but were trapped on a small piece of land by water.  Several hours later, they were rescued.

Officials in Des Plaines urged residents along the Des Plaines River to evacuate as waters rose to near record levels.  An estimated 25 residents of the Big Bend Drive area were rescued by firefighters using boats.  Other rescues occurred on Berry Lane and Mill Street.  River Road was closed through Des Plaines and Mt. Prospect.  Many roads in River Forest were closed.
Extensive flooding closed roads and inundated large areas near the river.  A levee break caused extensive flooding of homes in Sumava Resorts.
Extensive flooding closed roads and inundated large areas near the river.  A levee break caused extensive flooding of homes in Sumava Resorts.
The Little Calumet River reached the third highest crest on record, 20.16 feet, at South Holland on the 15th.  Many roads were flooded near the river.

Record flooding occurred along the Little Calumet River and its tributaries in northwest Indiana.  A record crest of 17.32 feet was set at Munster on the 14th.  Record flooding also occurred along Hart Ditch.  Nearly 190 patients were evacuated from the Munster Med-Inn.  Major flooding was reported in Munster with over a thousand homes evacuated as a levee along the Little Calumet River failed.  Interstate 80/94 was closed in northwest Indiana when levees were topped by flood waters.

The Illinois River reached a record crest of 24.84 feet at Morris on the 16th.  In Morris, flood waters inundated large areas near the river including the public works facilities and sewage treatment facilities.  Water surrounded Ravine Woods apartment complex and residents had to be evacuated.  Residents were also evacuated from homes on the east side of Morris along Cemetery Road.

The Illinois River reached a record crest of 33.79 feet at LaSalle on the 16th.  Major flooding occurred along the river in LaSalle County. In Marseilles, flood waters inundated Illini State Park and nearby areas.  Flood waters inundated the Peru power plant.  Brunner and Water Streets were closed due to flooding.  Navigation on the river was halted as most lock facilities were submerged.  The Interstate 39 bridge was the only one open as State Highways 251, 351, and 178 were closed.  Homes and businesses in Utica were flooded.  In Ottawa, 89 residents of a nursing home were evacuated.  Dee Bennett Road between Ottawa and Utica was closed.  Central Elementary School in Ottawa was surrounded by water and the auditorium was flooded with 8 inches of water.

After heavy rain and flash flooding across much of southern Cook County from the early morning through the afternoon of September 13th, flooding continued across many locations through the evening hours and into the early morning hours of September 14th, when another wave of heavy rain moved across the area.  A elderly man fell head first into a flooded window well and drowned in Oak Lawn.  He was trying to clear a plugged drain in the window well.

A combination of melting snow and heavy rain caused flash flooding across much of Dupage County.  Basement flooding was reported in Naperville, Addison and Elmhurst.  Many streets were closed due to flooding in Wheaton, Westmont, Glen Ellyn, Downers Grove, Carol Stream, Naperville, Villa Park, Lisle, Warrenville, and Willowbrook.  Stormtotal rainfall amounts included 2.19 inches near Downers Grove, 1.95 inches near Westmont, 1.95 inches near Wheaton, 1.82 inches near Lisle and 1.66 inches near Carol Stream.

Numerous roads were reported to be flooded and closed across eastern Ogle County, including Route 72 near Davis Junction, Route 251 south of Route 64 and Route 2 north of Bryon.  Stormtotal rainfall amounts included 1.48 inches 3 miles north of Bryon and 1.18 inches near Rochelle.
Many roads across eastern Lee County were flooded, some were closed.  Ditches and creeks were also flooded.  Stormtotal rainfall amounts included 1.88 inches near Dixon and 1.44 inches near Paw Paw.
Ten inch diameter tree limbs were blown down near Route 18 and East 9th Road.
A wind gust to 63 mph was measured southwest of Gibson City.
A farmer reported buildings and vehicles moved on his property by strong winds near Ashkum.
Wind gusts were estimated to 60 mph.
Collins Road between Plainfield Road and Grove Road was flooded and impassable.  Stormtotal rainfall amounts included 1.99 inches about one mile west of Yorkville and 1.93 inches near Plano.
Flood water was reported up to the foundations of several homes and was flowing over several roads.  A tributary was one foot above the Adams Road bridge.

Street flooding was reported in Rockford with ditches and culverts full.  Stormtotal rainfall amounts included 1.50 inches at Rockford Airport, 1.39 inches about 3 miles northeast of Rockford and 1.24 inches near Roscoe.
Six feet of water was reported on 135th Street between Central and Harlem.
After heavy rain and melting snow caused widespread flooding and flash flooding across Dupage County on December 27th, flooding continued on December 28th as flood waters slowly receded.
Heavy rain and melting snow caused flooding of some roads, creeks and low lying areas across southern Cook County on December 27th.  The flood waters slowly receded on December 28th.
Heavy rain and melting snow caused flooding of some roads, creeks and low lying areas across central and northern Cook County on December 27th.  The flood waters slowly receded on December 28th.
Two utility poles and several power lines were blown down on North Pine Street.

Several garage doors were blown out on Harrison Avenue.  Several buildings had shingles torn off.  One building suffered signifcant roof damage.  A construction trailer was blown onto its side, partially crushing a parked car.  Many tree limbs and power lines, which were still coated with ice from a recent ice storm, were blown down.
Numerous basements were flooded in Highland Park.  Several roads were also flooded including Trailway Street, Green Bay Road and Park Avenue.

Heavy rain fell across much of Dupage County causing flash flooding.  Widespread street flooding was reported.  In Wheaton, Main Street was closed due to flooding between Roosevelt Road and Illinois Street.  In Warrenville, Winfield Road was closed due to flooding between Butterfield and Warrenville Roads.  In Glendale Heights, Bloomingdale Road was closed due to flooding at Army Trail Road.  North of Carol Stream, a sewer cap burst at the corner of Mohican and Pocahantas causing flooding.  In Naperville, a man and child had to be rescued from their swamped vehicle after they tried to drive through floodwaters beneath a railroad overpass at Naper Boulevard.  Around the same time, three vehicles and their occupants became stuck in floodwater in the Elgin, Joliet & Eastern Railway underpass near the intersection of North Aurora and Frontenac roads.  Motorists were also reported stranded in floodwater in the 1000 block of East Gartner Road and Prairie Avenue and Julian Street.  Basement flooding was also reported in Naperville.  Rainfall totals included 2.16 inches in Carol Stream, 2.10 inches near Lisle and 2.02 inches in Oak Brook.
Golf Road was closed due to flooding between River Road and Route 21.
Bryn Mawr Avenue exit from Lake Shore Drive was flooded and closed.

After heavy rain and flash flooding late in the evening of February 26th and early in the morning of February 27th, flooding continued across many parts of Dupage County, especially along creeks, streams and rivers.

Heavy rain caused flooding across parts of northern Will County late in the evening of February 26th.  Flooding continued through February 28th, especially along creeks, streams and rivers.  Weber Road between Royce and Boughton Roads was closed due to flooding from the East Branch of the Dupage River.

After heavy rain and flash flooding late in the evening of February 26th and early in the morning of February 27th, flooding continued across many parts of north central Cook County, especially along creeks, streams and rivers.
Nickel size hail was reported near mile marker 308 on Interstate 57.
A wind gust to 59 mph was estimated near mile marker 308 on Interstate 57.
A wind gust to 60 mph was estimated near mile marker 303 on Interstate 57.

High winds damaged a brand new, 10,000 foot greenhouse and flattened and damaged 30,000 perennials.  The high winds also blew plastic roofs off some 30 separate plant buildings and took the roof off of a pole barn.  A grain auger was flipped over and damaged.  A large barn on N 11000 E Road was blown over and destroyed. A large tree was blown down.

An EF0 tornado touched down on county road 1500N between 1100E and 1200E.  A detached garage was destroyed at this location and the debris was deposited in a field to the northeast.  A hay barn at this same location suffered little damage although a trailer camper parked inside the barn was pushed through the wooden front door by straight line winds which were funneled through the open back of the barn.

An EF1 tornado touched down near the intersection of county roads 5000N and 7500E.  On the southwest corner of this intersection, a detached garage and steel shed were destroyed.  A two foot diameter tree was snapped at the base and several other trees had large branches broken off.  Debris from this location was lifted and carried approximately 100 yards into the field across the road.  The tornado also damaged property on the northeast corner of the intersection.  A corn crib and a shed which served as a blacksmith forge were both destroyed.  Debris from these buildings was scattered to the northeast in a narrow path approximately 800 yards long.  Corn stalks in a field to the northeast appeared to have been flattened and twisted by this tornado.

A tornado touched down at a farm about one half mile east of the intersection of county roads 8000N and 9000E.  Two barns at this location lost part of their roof.  Another garage and another steel building were completely destroyed.  Debris from this location was lifted and deposited in a field and treeline approximately 400 yards to the northeast.
High standing water was reported on all lanes of Interstate 94 at Cottage Grove Avenue.
A viaduct was briefly closed at 1800 North Ashland.
Nine inches of standing water was reported at Whittier and Glenwood.
Up to six inches of standing water was reported near Route 53 and Caton Farm Road.
Archer Avenue at 135th Street was flooded and almost impassible.

Flooding was reported on rural roads outside of Peotone.  Standing water of 8 to 10 inches was reported on Joliet Road one half mile east of Interstate 57.  Standing water of 4 to 5 inches was reported on north Peotone Road one quarter mile west of Harlem.
Part of 135th Street between Harlem and Central was flooded and closed.
Longwood Avenue between 108th and 110th was closed due to flooding.

Flooding occurred across many areas in Dupage County.  In Downers Grove, Webster Creek overflowed its banks; Basement flooding was reported; Fairview at Maple and Prairie was closed due to flooding; Five inches of standing water was reported on 63rd Street, east of Woodward.  In Carol Stream, Klein Creek overflowed its banks with street flooding reported.  In Wheaton, Main Street was flooded north of Route 38.
Tree limbs and power lines were blown down.
A semi truck was blown over at US 41 and US 52.
High standing water was reported on both sides of Interstate 80/94 near Kennedy Avenue.
Tree limbs were blown down along Illinois Route 113 and Tower Road.  Power lines were blown down near 4000N just north of 6000E.
A trailer park south of Remington had to be evacuated due to rising flood waters.  Rainfall of 1.45 inches was measured in 3.5 hours in Remington.
Flowing flood water several inches deep was reported over roads in northwest Benton County.  Earl Park measured a storm total of 3.1 inches of rain with 1.5 inches in 3 hours.
Ditches and fields were reported to be flooded along with standing water on some roads.  Storm total rainfall was measured at 1.81 inches in Kankakee.
Old Route 45 was closed due to flooding from Clifton to Chebanse.
Route 1 viaduct in Milford was flooded with 9 feet of water.  Drivers from two cars had to be rescued from their flooded cars.
Tree limbs and power lines were blown down.
Power lines were blown down on Sheridan Street in Winnetka.
A garage was destroyed.  A roof was blown off a building and trees were blown down.
A wind gust to 67 mph was measured at Rockford Airport.
Trees and power lines were blown down.  A well built shed was destroyed with debris scattered over 100 yards downstream.
Extensive tree damage was reported in Roscoe.  The roof of one home was damaged, as well as a fence.  A second home sustained roof and siding damage.  Power lines were also blown down.
A small yard barn was damaged.
A utility pole was blown over near Route 23 and 34th Road.
A sign was blown down at 95th Street and Clifton Park Avenue.  Large tree limbs and power lines were also blown down.
One airplane was flipped over and five other airplanes were damaged at Chicago Executive Airport.
