Trees were blown down on Cobb Street.  A 12 to 16 inch diameter tree was uprooted and fell onto a car.  The driver was not injured.  Three large trees were blown down on Main Street near the hospital, along with many large tree limbs.  Tree limbs and power lines were blown down across much of the city of Kankakee.  A large tree was uprooted and fell onto a house on Nelson Avenue causing severe damage to the first and second floors of the house.  Several large tree limbs were blown onto a house on South Seventh Avenue.
Minor street flooding was reported in Glen Ellyn.  Nearby rainfall reports included 1.52 inches near Lisle and 1.29 inches in Oak Brook.
Up to 8 inches of standing water was reported on roads near Illinois Valley Community College.
Several creeks in the town of Mendota were near bankfull.  Several intersections were closed due to flooding on the roadways.
The Green River was reported out of its banks in the Amboy area.  Low areas including fields were flooded with 2 to 3 feet of standing water on the east and southeast side of Amboy.
Water was reported flowing over multiple locations on Route 23, southeast of Waterman.
Street flooding was reported at the intersection of Pine Avenue and Mensching Road.  Goose Lake Park was reported to be under water from flooding.

The intersection of Kuhn Road and Birchbark Trail was closed due to water flowing onto the street from a retention pond.  Storm total rainfall of 1.87 inches was measured about a mile west of Carol Stream.
Water was reported on roads, and ditches were full from heavy rain.

Numerous streets were flooded across north central Cook County.  Water up to 4 inches deep was reported on Interstate 94 between Dundee and Willow Roads near Northbrook.  Water up to car bumpers was reported on McCormick between Touhy and Howard near Skokie.  Water was reported covering Main Street in Melrose Park.  Water 6 inches deep was reported at North Avenue and Damen in Chicago.  Storm total rainfall amounts included 1.88 inches about a mile south of Evanston; 1.88 inches at Chicago O'Hare Airport; 1.75 inches in Morton Grove; 1.63 inches about a mile south of Winnetka and 1.12 inches two miles northwest of Melrose Park.
Water up to 4 inches deep was reported along parts of Route 47 near Elburn.  Storm total rainfall of 3.13 inches was measured near Elburn.
A utility pole was blown down in a rural section of Lake Village, which brought down power lines.
Several trees were blown down in the Valparaiso area.
A tree was blown down along Baums Bridge Road.
A two foot diameter tree was blown down near Mill Street and Route 2, bringing down power lines.  Other tree damage was reported in Lowell.
Dixie Highway was flooded and impassable with water up to car bumpers near the Balmoral Park Race Track.
Strong winds developed behind a line of thunderstorms across the Rockford area.  A baseball dugout and field fencing was damaged at a school on North Alpine Road.
Four inches of water was reported on Route 47, approximately a quarter mile north of Plato Center.
The intersection of Dundee Road and Golfview Lane was flooded.  Two inches of rain fell over the hour leading up to this report.
A woman in Jackson Township was injured when lightning struck nearby while she was closing a metal window.
Water was overflowing many streets in Pontiac after 1.12 inches of rain fell in 30 minutes.

This is a continuation of a tornado that started in Ogle County and crossed into Winnebago County on East Montague Road near South Conger Road.  The path was nearly continuous briefly lifting near Kelly Road east of just Alworth Road, then continuing again into the west side of Machesney Park past the Kennedy Middle School which had part of its roof blown off.  A persistent path of damage was observed until the end of the tornado���s life when damage became sporadic.  Several damage indicators indicating a persistent EF1 rating were observed throughout the tornado���s path.  There were numerous softwood trees snapped or uprooted, some up to 24-30 inches in diameter.  A few hardwood trees up to 18 inches in diameter were also snapped. Many tree limbs were also downed.  Structural damage included several collapsed outbuildings, damaged siding and fascia to homes, and shingles blown off roofs.  Debris in numerous locations was deposited downstream from its origin, sometimes up to 400 yards.  All of the damage suggested winds from 90-110 mph.

Over a 12 hour period, 4.30 inches of rain was measured in Lostant causing ditches along Highway 251 to fill and overflow.  Two to three inches of water was on North 14th Road, and the eastbound lane of Illinois Route 18 had four to six inches of water.

events.event_narrative: A trained spotter on the third floor of a building located near Wood Street and Archer Avenue observed a rope shaped waterspout just off the Chicago lakefront, south of Northerly Island, which lasted for a few minutes.
Utility poles were snapped off east of Crescent City.
A house was struck by lightning in the 200 block of South Clyde Avenue in Palatine.  Most of the damage to the house was confined to the exterior.
Lightning struck a house in the 800 block of Fremont Avenue, which started a fire in the attic.
Hail up to the size of golf balls pounded the city of Roberts damaging numerous cars and roofs.
A semi truck was blown off of Route 47, about four miles south of Sibley.
Lightning struck a house on Scottsdale Circle which ignited the second floor roof.  The house was deemed uninhabitable.
Deerpath Road was closed under the Route 41 overpass due to flash flooding.
Numerous streets were flooded in Park Ridge.  Burton and Fenton Roads were completely impassable due to flood waters.
Half of a tree was blown down on North Fair Street.
Several storage buildings sustained roof damage near Route 251 and Rockton Road.

A two story, eight unit apartment building was struck by lightning.  The roof was engulfed in flames and the building was a total loss.  All of the 15 occupants were able to exit the building safely and no injuries were reported.
The roof of a barn was damaged between Donovan and Beaverville.  Tree damage was also reported near Beaverville.

Several inches of flowing water was reported on many streets in Peru including Green, Calhoun, Second and Water Streets.  U.S. Route 6 was closed for a short time due to flooding.  A manhole cover was lifted up and out of its fitting onto First Street in LaSalle.  Storm total rainfall of 3.52 inches was measured in LaSalle.
Lightning struck a garage on Roosevelt Road.  About an hour later, smoke was seen billowing from the detached garage.  The fire was quickly put out by firefighters.

Approximately 100 acres of farmland was flooded in the Earlville and Leland areas.  The young plants in these areas did not survive because they had been under water for too long.  Some of this land was expected to be replanted.  Storm total rainfall of 2.94 inches was measured three miles south of Earlville.
Shingles were torn off the roof of a home just north of Route 30 in Shabbona.  Tree limbs were also blown down nearby.

Several feet of water flooded the Laurel Avenue underpass at First Street where two cars were stranded in the flood waters.  Flooding was also reported at the Sheridan Road entrance to Rosewood Beach.  Many other streets were flooded with standing water in Highland Park.

Flooding was reported in many areas in and around Niles including flooding at a golf course on Howard Road and flooding at the Gemini Junior High School on Greenwood.  Storm total rainfall was measured at 2.80 inches.
Lightning struck a four story apartment building on Summit Drive causing damage to the roof and attic.
A semi truck rolled over on Interstate 57 near Clifton.
Lightning struck a pig-confined building along Kelley Road in Pecatonica.  The damage was confined to the utility room and no livestock was lost.
Large tree limbs and power lines were blown down.
Tree limbs, utility poles and power lines were blown down in many areas of Machesney Park.
A large tree was blown down onto a building near Route 251 and New Milford School Road.  A nearby building suffered significant damage when a 50 foot ash tree fell onto the building.
Hail to the size of half dollars was reported near Pine Avenue and Thompson Road.

Hail from marble size to golfball size was reported.

Sustained winds of 48 to 50 mph with peak gusts to 58 mph occurred at the intersection of 91st Street and Clifton Park.
A five inch diameter tree fell onto a home near Home Avenue and Ridgeland Avenue.

A wind gust to 70 mph was estimated near White Oak and 181st Avenues.

The National Weather Service conducted an aerial survey and determined that the damage was spread out across a path approximately two miles wide.  All trees and debris appeared to be blown down in the same direction, to the southeast.||The most intense damage occurred from just east of Interstate 65 and Route 2 southeast toward the Kankakee River and the Lake Porter county line.  A semi truck was blown over near exit 240 and part of the roof of a weigh station was blown off near mile marker 243, both on Interstate 65.  Hundreds of large trees were snapped or uprooted.  Some detached garages, farm outbuildings and grain bins were destroyed or severely damaged.  Homes suffered some loss of shingles.  There were five metal tress electrical towers collapsed near Route 2 and Clay Street.  Although the EF guide would suggest stronger winds may be required to collapse the towers, none of the other nearby observed damage was consistent with wind speeds higher than around 110 mph.
Several trees and tree limbs were blown down in and around Wheatfield.
A wind gust to 78 mph was measured in Earl Park.  Several trees were blown down or uprooted including a 30 inch diameter tree that was snapped off 3 feet from its base.
Numerous trees and power lines were blown down across southern Benton County.
Many trees and power lines were blown down across southern Lake County.

Route 2 from Lake County into Porter County was impassable due to numerous trees and utility poles blown down.  As many as 60 trees were either damaged or blown down in Hebron.  Trees and structures were damaged along 900S.
Five utility poles were blown down.
Large trees were blown down near Kay Street and Route 24.

Strong winds blew shingles off the roof of a house and snapped a 3-inch diameter 6-foot tall tree about one foot above the ground.  Nearby towns of South Beloit and Machesney Park measured 55 mph gusts.
Strong winds caused a tree limb of unknown size to fall onto a car.
A 6 inch diameter tree was snapped near the 7800 block of Mildred Road. A 10 inch diameter tree was downed near the intersection of Wilson Avenue and Waterview Road.
A 6 inch diameter tree was snapped near the intersection of Alpine Road and Harrison Avenue.
Heavy rains caused road closures along Route 30 between 127th Street and 135th Street.  At the National Weather Service in Romeoville, a storm total of 5.29 inches of rain was measured.

Heavy rain caused Governors Highway just south of Stuenkel Road to become impassible with several inches of flowing water.  One car became stalled on the side of the road.  A trained spotter reported 3.41 inches of rain.
Several tree limbs were knocked onto power lines and some large limbs fell onto the roads blocking traffic.
Multiple powerlines were reported down.
Multiple large tree limbs were reported down across the town of Watseka.

The tornado began at approximately 518 PM CST at the Bishop Ford Expressway north of 159th Street.  The tornado ended at 520 PM CST near the intersection of 158th Place and Paxton Avenue.  It had a path length of 0.8 miles and a width of about 20 yards.  The tornado was rated EF0 with winds 65 to 85 mph.  The first signs of damage were at the Brown Meat Packing Company on Dutch Valley Road.  The tornado caused damage to the roof of the meat packing plant.  A 40 foot by 60 foot section of roofing was torn off and pieces of the roof were thrown 150 to 250 feet to the left of the tornado path, indicating rotation.  An air conditioning unit was flipped and roof debris damaged a brick parapet.  There was damage to a few shingles at the Sand Ridge Apartments on 158th Place.  A few small tree limbs were also damaged.  Debris from the roof of the plant also fell around the apartment complex.

A large tree was blown down blocking portions of Route 12 near the intersection of Quentin Road causing damage to a wrought iron fence in Kildeer. Near Beach Park, numerous tree branches were blown down, and a portion of northbound Green Bay Road was blocked by a large branch. Winds gusting to 54 mph and 45 mph were measured in Libertyville and Waukegan, respectively.
Tree limbs and power lines were blown down.

The survey team reported a housing residence along Route 17 that had a shed completely destroyed, with the walls collapsed and the roof blown approximately 25 feet away.  There was extensive hardwood tree damage for most of the damage path.  Most of the trees damaged were either uprooted or snapped off at the base.  These were large, mostly healthy trees.  There were several trees where the break was a third to half of the way up the tree trunk.  One of the housing structures along 7000W had a glass window blown out.  An additional building had damage in the siding from a branch piercing the outer wall.  Along 2000N, there were several occurrences of damage to man-made objects at several homesteads.  The door on a large tin barn was blown into the structure and several panels of the siding collapsed.  On the same property, a wooden corn shed was completely destroyed, and a house sustained shingle damage.  A metal siding fence also blew down on the property line, as well as a chain link fence.  Another property on 2000N incurred heavy structural damage due to fallen trees.  Along the damage path, there were convergent wind patterns in several corn and wheat fields.  In addition, the fallen trees laid in a convergent pattern.  Many branches were speared into the ground in a convergent pattern, as well.  The nature of this damage was consistent with an EF1 tornado with winds of 100 to 110 mph.
Water more than 6 inches deep was moving cars as it flowed over portions of Route 71 near North 2401 Road and North 2650 Road.
Three large trees were reported down across roadways in rural areas between two and five miles northwest of Mount Ayr.
A tree was downed near the intersection of Route 9 and 1600 E.
Winds gusting to 60 mph was measured on Interstate 39 approximately one mile north of Route 18.
A wind gust to 71 mph was measured in Pontiac.  Several tree limbs were blown down, some onto power lines.
Winds gusts were estimated to 60 mph near the intersection of Normantown Road and Hudson Avenue.
Estimated gusts to 65 mph occurred one block south of Four Seasons Boulevard and Victoria Park Circle.
Estimated 65 mph winds occurred near the intersection of Caton Farm Road and Essington Road.
Transformers exploded when an estimated 75 mph gust occurred near the intersection of Roosevelt Road and County Farm Road.
Winds gusting to 66 mph were measured at the Lewis University Airport AWOS and 60 mph at the National Weather Service office nearby.
A 15 inch diameter tree was split down the middle with a 6 inch diameter branch broken off.

A National Weather Service storm survey confirmed an EF1 tornado touched down near Sunnydale Park and lifted near 55th and Main in Downers Grove.  Most of the damage was to trees.  Many mature hardwood trees had been snapped or knocked down.  A fence was blown down at Downers Grove High School. An estimated 35 homes were damaged by falling trees.
Small trees were blown down.

Winds were estimated between 60 and 75 mph across portions of east-central DuPage County causing numerous branches to fall and power outages.  A large tree fell onto Route 53 approximately one mile north of Roosevelt Road blocking the northbound lane in Lombard.  A 14 inch diameter tree fell onto a car near the intersection of Fordham Way and Longford Drive in Westmont.  Also in Westmont, a neighborhood near 55th Street and Clarendon Hills Road had numerous 10 inch diameter or greater tree limbs blown down.  A garage was heavily damaged by a falling tree in Elmhurst and a large tree was snapped off at its base on Berteau in Elmhurst.
Emergency managers in DuPage County measured 62 mph wind gusts in Wheaton while a mesonet just north of Wheaton measured 59 mph wind gusts.
Local media reported that two people were in serious to critical condition after their car was crushed by a falling tree near the intersection of Farragut Avenue and Leavitt Street.
Three medium sized trees were blown over.
Approximately 50 trees were blown down or damaged in Oak Lawn.  Numerous tree limbs were also blown down.  Wind gusts were estimated between 70 and 80 mph.
Significant tree damage was reported with two to three foot diameter trees uprooted and blown down.  Some of the trees fell onto houses.  Minor sign damage was reported to a business on 95th Street.

Several trees approximately two feet in diameter were blown down, some blocking streets.  Several utility poles were either blown down or snapped off at their base.  Numerous tree limbs and power lines were blown down.  The roof of a house on Fourth Street was damaged when a chimney was blown down and fell onto the roof.  The roof of another house on Fourth Street was damaged by a falling tree.  A large tree was blown down near South Fifth and Locust.
Wind gusts were estimated to 60 mph.
Hail 1.5 inches in diameter was reported in University Park.
Wind gusts were estimated to 60 mph in University Park.
Quarter size hail was reported near Route 1 and Crete-Monee Road.
Nickel size hail was reported near Irving Park Road and Lake Shore Drive.
Hail 1.5 inches in diameter was reported near Erie Street and Racine Avenue.
Half dollar size hail was reported in the Lakeview neighborhood.
Hail 2.0 inches in diameter was reported in Logan Square.
Quarter size hail was reported in Ravenswood.
Hail 2.0 inches in diameter was reported near 26th Street and Pulaski Road.
Hail 2.0 inches in diameter was reported near 5th Avenue and Pulaski Road.

Hail as large as baseballs was reported near 26th Street and Kedzie Avenue.  Hundreds of vehicles were damaged including at least 130 police cars that suffered broken windshields and smashed rooftop lights.

events.event_narrative: Damaged boats were reported at North Point Marina including torn sails.
Trees greater than 12 inches in diameter and light poles were blown down at North Point Marina.
Numerous large trees were uprooted or blown down in Zion along with tree limbs and power lines.

events.cz_name: WINTHROP HARBOR TO WILMETTE HARBOR IL
events.event_narrative: A waterspout was reported east of Zion.
In Beach Park, a tree fell onto a car and structural damage was reported to a house after a tree fell on it.
Over 1,000 trees were either uprooted or split in half at the Illinois Beach State Park.  Various structures as well as mobile campers sustained damage from the falling trees.

Hail 2.0 inches in diameter shattered thousands of glass panes at the Garfield Park Conservatory.  Clean up costs were estimated at $2 million while repair and replacement costs were estimated at $15 million.
A 14 inch diameter tree fell on a car near Fordham Way and Longford Drive.
A 14 inch diameter tree was uprooted near the intersection of Fairview Avenue and Gierz Street.
The top of a 6 to 8 inch diameter maple tree was snapped off near Cass Avenue and 63rd Street.
Numerous tree limbs were blown down near 55th Street and Clarendon Hills Road.  Some tree limbs were 10 inches or greater in diameter.
Multiple whole trees were blown down northeast of Cumberland Parkway.
Tree limbs as large as 18 inches in diameter were blown down between the intersections of 63rd and Main Street and 59th Street and Fairview.  Structural damage was also reported to roofs.

Numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown.  Some trees and limbs fell on cars causing damage.  A 40 foot tall tree was completely uprooted on Kolmar Street and fell onto a house.  Twelve inch diameter tree limbs were blown down near Skokie Village Hall.

Several large trees were blown down near Dempster Street, approximately two blocks east of Interstate 94.  One tree fell onto a car.  Several 12 inch diameter trees were uprooted near the intersection of Laramie Avenue and Golf Road.
Wind gusts were estimated to 70 mph.  Numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down in Morton Grove.
Wind gusts were estimated to 60 mph in Des Plaines with multiple large tree limbs blown down near the intersection of Golf Road and Wolf Road.

A tornado touched down near the intersection of We Go Trail and Golf Road and moved north-northeast before lifting near the intersection of North Pine Street and Kensington Road.  Most of the damage was fallen trees, a few of which fell onto houses causing structural damage.  An estimated 2,000 trees were damaged in Mt. Prospect with 130 completely blown down or that needed to be removed.  Most of the tree damage was in and near the path of the tornado.
A ramp from Farnsworth Avenue to Interstate 88 flooded with six inches of standing water.
Multiple intersections were flooded in the town of Amboy.
Middle Aux Sable Creek was out of its bank near Ashley Road.
Heavy rain caused 10 to 12 inches of standing water at the intersection of Dolores Street and Charles Court.
Heavy rain caused 4 to 8 inches of standing water on La Grange Road between 55th Street and Plainfield Road.

Heavy rain caused 4 to 12 inches of standing water on the southbound lanes of Interstate 55 approximately a quarter mile east of Route 83.  An observer in nearby Oak Brook measured a storm total rainfall of 2.58 inches.
Heavy rain caused 5 to 10 inches of standing water at the intersection of Joliet Road and Bluff Road.

Heavy rain caused 4 to 8 inches of standing water on Route 53, approximately a third of a mile north of Taylor Road.  The National Weather Service in Romeoville measured a storm total rainfall of 5.29 inches.
High standing water was reported at the intersection of 103rd Street and Central Avenue.
Heavy rain measuring 2.74 inches caused 8 inches of standing water at the intersection of North Peotone Road and Center Road.

Wind gusts to 81 mph were measured at Chicago Executive Airport.  Roof damage was reported to three hangers.  Four airplanes were damaged, with two of them flipped over.  Approximately 1,000 feet of fencing was destroyed.  A willow tree was uprooted on Wolf Road in Wheeling.
Estimated wind gusts to 70 mph occurred in Schaumburg.
Heavy rain caused 5 to 6 inches of standing water at the intersection of County Road 15 and County Road 30.
Wind gusts were estimated to 60 mph.  Tree limbs and power lines were blown down.
Wind gusts were estimated to 65 mph.
Wind gusts were estimated to 60 mph.
The sidewall of an aluminum shed was blown down.
Several tree limbs 6 to 14 inches in diameter were blown down near Milwaukee Avenue and Lake Cook Road.
Wind gusts were estimated to 60 mph.
Wind gusts were estimated to 60 mph approximately one mile north of Interstate 94 on Bradley Road.
Wind gusts were estimated to 60 mph near the intersection of North Avenue and Ridgeland Avenue where multiple 30-foot long branches were blown down.
Golfball size hail was reported near Route 30 and 135th Street as well as one mile west of Plainfield.  Penny size hail was reported in numerous areas in and around Plainfield.
Trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down in many areas.  Some trees fell onto houses and other buildings.  Power outages lasted several days causing significant food spoilage.
Numerous large trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down.  Several roads were blocked by the fallen trees.
A house was struck by lightning on Carol Street causing extensive structural damage.
A tree was blown down on Gray Street.  Tree limbs and power lines were also blown down in parts of Geneva.
A roof was blown off a building on Waveland.  Part of the roof was tangled in nearby power lines.
A 100 foot tall maple tree was blown down onto a house causing signficant damage to the roof and attic.

High winds blew over several bleachers, blew down a fence along with many downed trees in Redmond Park.  Numerous trees and tree limbs were blown down in parts of Bensenville.  Some of the trees fell onto cars.
The top of a huge tree was snapped off and crashed through part of a bedroom of a house causing significant damage.
Part of the roof of a building on Malmo Drive was ripped off.
Tree limbs, utility poles and power lines were blown down.  A large tree limb fell on a parked car causing significant damage.
A large section of a tree was blown down narrowly missing a house.
A 14 inch diameter, 20 foot long tree limb fell on a porch on Ashland Avenue.  Several homes and at least one car were damaged.

Trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down.  Over 100 trees were blown down or needed to be completely removed.  Numerous grocery stores and restaurants had to rent refrigerated trucks or ship perishable items to warehouses due to extended power outages.  Three cars were damaged by falling tree limbs including one on Neva Avenue, one on Touhy Avenue and a one on Oakton Street.

A huge oak tree was uprooted along 26th Place in Brookfield.  The tree fell on top of a house, but all of the large limbs remained in the air and no damage was reported to the roof.  Additional trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down in Brookfield.
A large tree was blown down near the Rosemont Fitness Center.  Part of the tree damaged 8 feet of chain link fence.  Other tree limbs were blown down.
Tree limbs and power lines were blown down.

Trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down in many areas in Prospect Heights.  A large tree was completely uprooted along the Willow Sloughs.  The roof of an apartment building on Wolf Road was blown off.
Tree limbs and power lines were blown down.
Five trees were blown down across parts of Bluff Road.  Other tree limbs and power lines were blown down.
Numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down.  Many trees fell onto houses and garages.  The roof of an apartment building on Chestnut Street was blown off.
Tree limbs and power lines were blown down.

The west side of La Grange was hit the hardest with numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines blown down.  Some streets were completely blocked due to the fallen trees.  Six homes and one garage were damaged by the falling trees and limbs and at least one vehicle was damaged.

Tree limbs and power lines were blown down in Highland Park.  A large tree was uprooted along Sheridan Road.  When a back-up generator kicked on at a water plant, it created a pressure surge that blew a fist-sized hole in a water main.

At least 50 trees were blown down with damage to hundreds of other trees.  Tree limbs fell onto houses and cars.  A transmission line that supplies electricity to the southern half of the city was also blown down, in addition to numerous other power lines.

In Harwood Heights, every block had either broken trees or tree limbs.  Some streets were completely blocked by fallen trees.  A few cars were damaged by fallen trees.  One car was damaged by a live powerline when it started a fire.  Numerous other powerlines were blown down.
A 35 foot by 40 foot section of an apartment building roof was blown off a multifamily residence on Josephine Street in Maine Township.

Numerous trees, tree limbs, utility poles and power lines were blown down.  A transformer was completely blown off a utility pole.  A large tree fell onto a house on Oakwood Street but only caused damage to the gutters.  Damage was also reported to netting and fencing at a golf course.
Hundreds of trees were damaged in and around the Buffalo Grove area.  Utility poles and power lines were also blown down.
Numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down.
Approximately 300 trees were damaged in Lake Forest with 35 trees blown down or were damaged severely enough to be removed.
Trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down.
Hundreds of trees were damaged in Villa Park.  About 20 mature trees were removed due to severe damage.
Numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down.  One tree fell onto a parked car on Keating Avenue.

Water 3 to 4 inches deep was reported along US 30 in Valparaiso.  Water from a flooded parking lot spilled into a floral shop.  Several streets were flooded.  The Porter County Municipal Airport southeast of Valparaiso measured a storm total of 3.97 inches of rain, with 2.27 inches of that total falling in one hour between 853am CST to 953am CST.
Several trees and power lines were blown down in Morris.  The most significant was on Liberty Street, where a tree fell onto a house causing damage.  Another tree fell and blocked Cemetery Road.
The City of Chicago Streets and Sanitation reported 1,120 tree emergencies, which can range from a tree limb blown down to an entire tree blown over or uprooted.
A one story home on Uncas Street was struck by lightning.  The fire and damage was confined to the living room and front door area.
A house was struck by lightning which started a fire.  The home suffered severe damage and was left unhabitable.
A gas station canopy at Ogden and Yackley Avenues was blown over, crushing three gas pumps.

Numerous streets were flooded in and around Wheaton.  Some streets were closed due to high standing water, including Main Street, where a car was stranded in flood waters.  Lake Ellyn in Glen Ellyn overflowed its banks and began flooding nearby areas.

A large tree was struck by lightning in an alley near Kennedy Drive and North Street.  The tree then fell on to three cars, destroying two of them.  Power lines were also brought down by the falling tree.
Lightning struck the chimney of a brick building near La Grange Road and Burlington Avenue.  Bricks and debris were scattered across the street and on sidewalks.
Street and basement flooding was reported in Ottawa.  Water in some basements was several feet deep.  A sink hole was found next to a driveway on Main Street.
A tree limb was blown down onto power lines on South Rawson Bridge Road between Three Oaks and Crystal Lakes roads.
Lightning struck a house in the 5300 block of East Wonder Lake Road and started a fire in the attic.
Lightning struck the chimney of a house on Herrick Road.  The chimney was destroyed.  The lightning apparently started a fire on the opposite side of the house, causing minimal additional damage.
A car was submerged in flood waters along US 231.  Street flooding as well as standing water was reported.
Flooding was reported in and around Lowell including several feet of flood waters at a parking lot near Interstate 65 where several vehicles were stranded.
A large tree was completely uprooted along 68th Court.

Torrential rains between 4 and 5 inches left numerous roads and areas flooded in and around Orland Park and Palos Park.  Water was seen pouring out of storm drains and sewers.  Several roads were closed due to flooding and vehicles were stranded in flood waters along Route 83 and 127th Street.

Over 60 streets and 1,000 basements were flooded in and around the 19th Ward of the City of Chicago.  Numerous cars were stranded in the flood waters.  The force of the flood waters caused sewers to explode on 105th Street.
At least 57 trees were blown down in and around the Beverly area.
Tree limbs and power lines were blown down.
Minor street flooding along with some basement flooding was reported.  Storm total rainfall amounts of 1.50 inches were measured in Marseilles.

Indiana Dunes State Park campsites were flooded with two to three inches of standing water.  Roads were covered with three to four inches of water.  Park officials measured a storm total of 4.0 inches of rainfall.

events.event_narrative: Portions of a corn field were flattened near Harmon Road and Rock Island Road.

A semi-truck was overturned in Loves Park on Perryville Road between Harlem Road and Mulford Road.  State Street was closed from 9th Street to Division after a large tree was blown down taking down power lines.  Rockford Park District reported that 25 parks and facilities sustained some type of storm damage, mostly from fallen trees.
Winds were estimated to 60 mph outside of WREX television studio.
Winds estimated to 70 mph blew down 12-inch diameter trees, including one that fell onto the roadway blocking Spring Street.

In the town of Creston, two large trees were blown down and three telephone poles were leaning.  Corn in the area was flattened.  A metal barn was blown over halfway between Malta and Creston on the north side of Route 38.

events.event_narrative: Several trees 10 to 14 inches in diameter were blown down.
Trees were blown down blocking the westbound lane of West State Street near Weldon Road.
Wind gusts were estimated as high as 80 mph at the WREX Studios.
A large tree was blown down blocking southbound Meridian Road just north of US 20.
Several large trees were blown down in Sinnissippi Park near North 2nd Street and Ethel Avenue.

A boat of unknown size was tied to a dock along the Rock River near Arlington Street.  The boat was lifted out of the water and landed in a nearby tree.  Several windows were also reported blown out near Arlington Street.
Wind gusts were estimated to 70 mph two miles north northeast of Rockford.
Wind gusts were estimated to 80 mph near North Alpine and Spring Creek Roads.
Wind gusts were estimated to 70 mph near Court and John Streets.  A six inch diameter tree limb was blown down.
A wind gust to 71 mph was measured near Interstate 90 and Riverside Boulevard.
Wind gusts were estimated to 75 mph near State Street and Perryville Road.

Standing water up to 6 inches deep was reported in streets.  Vehicles were stranded in deep standing water on Charles Street near 9th Street, East State Street near Rockford Avenue, and at East State Street and New Towne Drive.

Numerous large trees were snapped and uprooted.  The hardest hit area was north of North Avenue, south of Aztec and between Kuhn Road and Gary Avenue.  The mayor declared Carol Stream a disaster.  Approximately 200 trees were damaged.
The roof of a muffler shop was damaged.  Debris and signs were blown down near North Avenue and along Summit Avenue.  Power lines were also blown down.

Many trees were blown down in Glen Ellyn including a tree that damaged a house and resulted in the closure of Park Boulevard.  Numerous large tree limbs and at least one uprooted tree were reported in a narrow swath of damage south of the railroad tracks and north of Roosevelt Road.
Extensive tree limb damage was reported throughout Mc Cook.  A large sign in front of a restaurant was pulled from its concrete base.  A utility pole was blown down across Joliet Road.
Several viaducts under Lake Shore Drive were flooded between Oak Street and Irving Park Road.
Street flooding was reported in Valparaiso with a vehicle stranded in flood waters.  Rainfall of 2.25 inches was reported in Valparaiso in approximately one and a half hours.
Numerous trees and power lines were blown down.  A limb fell on a vehicle.  Corn was flattened near town.
Wind gusts were estimated to 60 mph.
Corn fields were flattened, and 6-inch diameter branches were blown down along with power lines.
Power lines were blown down and were blocking eastbound lanes of Interstate 90 near Boone McHenry County Line Road.
Route 251 was blocked by downed power lines near Spur Road.
Winds gusting 70 to 80 mph damaged power transformers and blew over a semi-truck.

Over 30 large trees were reported down in the Poplar Grove and Candlewick Lake area, including one tree that fell onto a house on Bounty Drive in Candlewick Lake and a tree that fell onto a car in Poplar Grove.  Also in Poplar Grove, a roof was blown off of a house and a garage was destroyed.
Trees were snapped at the base just south of Route 38 on Annie Glidden Road.  Corn was flattened in areas surrounding De Kalb.

North Sheridan Road, south of West Wadsworth Road was closed for several hours due to standing water up to 8 inches deep.  Rainfall of 3.80 inches was reported one mile west of Beach Park at 930 am CST.
A tree and tree limbs were blown down.  Corn crops were also damaged.
A brief tornado touched down near 1300 S and Route 41.  No damage was reported.

Heavy rain fell across Lake County producing flash flooding in some areas.  Several roads were flooded in and around Beach Park with rapidly flowing water in drainage ditches.  Street flooding was also reported in Waukegan where all four lanes of Lewis Avenue were flooded by Bonnie Brook Golf Course.  The intersection of Sunset and Delany was closed due to flooding.  Six inches of flowing water was reported over the intersection of Highway 131 and Route 173.  Storm total rainfall amounts included 4.37 inches in Wadsworth; 3.93 inches two miles northeast of Gurnee; 3.32 inches at the Waukegan Regional Airport and 3.11 inches near Zion.
Lightning struck a lightning rod attached to a building.  Apparently, an employee was shocked as he opened a door to that building.  He was disoriented, but suffered no serious injuries.

The Chicago area experienced an intense heat wave in mid to late July. High temperatures at Chicago O'Hare were 95 on the 17th, 92 on the 18th, 93 on the 19th, 99 on the 20th, and 99 on the 21st. Low temperatures were mostly in the 70s. Thunderstorms brought some relief on the 22nd and 23rd but temperatures remained in the upper 80s through the 25th.
A teenage girl who was detassling corn in a field 6 miles east of Mendota became weak and dehydrated. Temperatures were in the 80s with high humidity. She required medical attention from paramedics.

Winds estimated to 70 mph caused several trees to snap.  One large oak tree fell onto a house and car, but damage to property was minimal.  The press box at DeKalb High School was blown over.  The building was secured by pilings set in concrete, which were pulled out of the ground.  Power lines were downed near Normal Road and 10th Street.  A tree limb fell onto a home and damaged the gas meter.  Portions of a corn field were flattened in Waterman.
Numerous 12-inch diameter trees and power lines were blown down.  Some trees were snapped.  One tree fall onto a house.
A roof was blown off of a house and a garage was destroyed.
Winds were estimated to 60 mph.
In the Meadowbrook neighborhood, there were numerous houses with the siding ripped off.  Multiple trees were uprooted or snapped at the base.  One house on Waterford Lake had the chimney blown off.
Winds to 65 mph were measured with an anemometer.  A tree was blown down on Beith Road.

Winds estimated to more than 70 mph lasted for two to three minutes causing 1-foot diameter trees and large branches to blow over as well as power outages.  Large limbs fell through the windshield of a car at an intersection on Dole Avenue.
Winds were estimated to 60 mph and caused damage to power transformers.

Fences were blown down and an 8-inch diameter tree was snapped near Hintz Road and Windsor Drive.  At Arlington Park Race Track, 4 to 6 inch diameter branches were blown down.  Numerous trees and power lines were also down across the area.  There was a report of a window blown out of a house.
Numerous tree limbs of up to 8 inches in diameter were blown down.
Wind gusts were estimated between 60 and 70 mph.
Wind gusts were estimated to 60 mph causing intermittent power failures.
A portion of a roof was peeled off by strong winds on Church Street.
Tree limbs of up to 4 inches in diameter were blown down.  Some large trees were snapped, blocking roads.
Large tree limbs were blown down.
Numerous large trees and tree limbs were blown over.  A traffic light on Naperville Road was blown down.
A 12-inch tree fell on a house near the intersection of Windsory Drive and Palatine Road.  An 18-inch tree was also uprooted nearby.

Thunderstorms produced torrential rainfall across northern Cook County with rainfall rates between 2 and 4 inches per hour which caused widespread flash flooding.  Chicago O'Hare Airport measured 6.78 inches of rain during a 3 hour period between 1251 am CDT and 351 am CDT, with 3.19 inches falling between 151 am CDT and 251 am CDT.  This extreme rainfall which fell across much of northern Cook County caused widespread street, parking lot and basement flooding with numerous cars stranded and submerged.  Retention ponds, creeks and small streams quickly overflowed their banks.||In Prospect Heights, a sewage lift station lost power for about 6 hours, causing the flooding to be worse in some areas.  Some basements were completely flooded with flood water and sewage 8 to 10 feet deep.  In Mt. Prospect, an estimated 100 vehicles were disabled in high water.  Numerous roads and intersections were flooded with several feet of standing water.  Two feet of water pooled in the underground parking garage of the Mt. Prospect Library.  Some of this water seeped into the lower level lobby.  In Park Ridge, nearly 500 basements were flooded along with numerous streets.  In nearby unincorporated Maine Township, more than 500 residences and 175 businesses were affected by flooding.  Hundreds of vehicles suffered some amount of flood damage with some vehicles completely covered by flood waters.||In Niles, more than 240 homes suffered some level of flooding with 5 to 6 feet of water in some basements.  In Glenview, three manhole covers were blown off by the flood waters with numerous flooded streets.  In Glencoe, numerous streets were flooded and impassible stranding dozens of cars.  One motorist needed to be rescued from a vehicle.  The basment of the Village Hall was also flooded.  In Des Plaines, dozens of streets and basements were flooded.  Some basements sustained as much as $10,000 in damages.  One woman had to be rescued from her stranded car on Elmhurst Road.  Fairgrounds in downtown Des Plaines were damaged by flood water.  In Northbrook, four motorists had to be rescued from vehicles stranded in flood waters.  In Elk Grove Village, almost every road had some amount of flooding during the height of the storm.  At least one vehicle was stranded in flood waters on Morrison Boulevard.||In Rolling Meadows, the Carriageway area and Barker Lake areas were the hardest hit.  Several streets were flooded with stranded and submerged vehicles.  In Winnetka, numerous streets were flooded and impassible with stranded and submerged vehicles.  Basement flooding was widespread.  A sink hole developed near a large hackberry tree and the water rushing into the hole resembled a small waterfall.  The tree began to lean over and was eventually cut down.  The Winnetka Golf Club's 18 hole course was closed for 10 days due to flooding and is part of a floodplain, which is expected to provide stormwater detention after heavy rain.  In Palatine, a 15 foot by 20 foot sinkhole developed at the northwest corner of Dundee and Hicks Road when a sewer line about 30 feet below the surface collapsed.  In Arlington Heights, numerous streets and basements were flooded including the parking lot of the International Plaza.  Several cars were stranded in the flood waters.  The Arlington Heights Chamber of Commerce office in the basement of a bank was flooded.  Flood water was reported to be a raging river which roared down Phelps Avenue in Arlington Heights.  Damage to just one basement was estimated at $80,000.||Storm total rainfall amounts included 8.20 inches at Chicago O'Hare Airport; 7.25 inches in Arlington Heights; 7.17 inches in Elk Grove Village; 6.06 inches at the Wheeling/Chicago Excutive Airport and 5.33 inches in Northbrook.

Thunderstorms produced torrential rainfall across central and southeast Cook County with rainfall rates between 2 and 4 inches per hour which caused widespread flash flooding.  Chicago O'Hare Airport measured 6.78 inches of rain during a 3 hour period between 1251 am CDT and 351 am CDT, with 3.19 inches falling between 151 am CDT and 251 am CDT.  This extreme rainfall which fell across much of central Cook County caused widespread street, parking lot and basement flooding with numerous cars stranded and submerged.  Retention ponds, creeks and small streams quickly overflowed their banks.||In Oak Park, at least 163 homes experenced basement flooding.  In Elmwood Park, several feet of water covered Oak Leaf Avenue with numerous cars stranded in the flood waters.  About eight cars were stalled out along 80th Avenue.  In La Grange, numerous vehicles were stranded and stalled in flood waters, including one police car.  The basement of the police station also flooded.  In Norridge, numerous streets and basements were flooded.  Several streets, underpasses and basements were flooded in and around Rosemont.  Several vehicles appeared to have been piled up by flood waters along Mannheim Road near O'Hare Airport.||In Chicago, hundreds of basements, roads and viaducts were flooded.  Some of the more significant reports included three semi trucks stranded in water more than 10 feet deep on Interstate 57 near 99th Street.  One of the three drivers swam away.  The other two drivers were rescued by boat.  Lakeshore Drive was closed between Chicago and Congress.  Interstate 94 was closed in both directions near 87th Street and northbound at 67th Street.  Hundreds of vehicles were stranded or stalled in flood waters.  Railroad tracks which service the Chicago Transportation Authority's Red, Blue and Pink lines were flooded.  Several motorists need to be rescued from strand cars in flood waters on the Edens Expressway at Willow Road.  The Metropolitan Water Reclamation District opened the locks at Wilmette and the Chicago River downtown, which allows untreated sewage and rain water to flow directly into Lake Michigan.||Storm total rainfall amounts included 8.20 inches at Chicago O'Hare Airport; 4.92 inches near Oak Park; 4.30 inches near Countryside and 4.00 inches in Melrose Park.

Lightning struck a 39 unit apartment building in Mt. Prospect.  The fire quickly consumed the attic and 3rd floor.  Fire departments were delayed by flooded roads.  The building was a total loss and would be demolished with all 75 residents having to find a new place to live.  Many of the residents lost all their belongings.
Lightning struck a house on Jackson Street which started a fire in the attic and on the second floor.  Damage to the house was estimated at $75,000 and at $25,000 to its contents.

Lightning struck a large house on Lincoln Avenue and started a fire in the attic which spread to the second floor.  The house and its contents were a total loss.  No one was home at the time of the fire.
A church on Division Street was struck by lightning which broke a hole in the steeple tower.  Much of the damage was from heavy rain which entered through the hole.

Thunderstorms produced torrential rainfall across northeast Dupage County with rainfall rates between 2 and 4 inches per hour which caused flash flooding.  Chicago O'Hare Airport measured 6.78 inches of rain during a 3 hour period between 1251 am CDT and 351 am CDT, with 3.19 inches falling between 151 am CDT and 251 am CDT.  This extreme rainfall which fell across northeast Dupage County caused street, parking lot and basement flooding in some areas.  Retention ponds, creeks and small streams quickly overflowed their banks.  A Bensenville man was rescued after his vehicle became stuck when he drove into a flooded construction zone.  Storm total rainfall amounts included 8.20 inches at Chicago O'Hare Airport; 3.68 inches in Villa Park; 3.60 inches in Glen Ellyn; 3.48 inches in Carol Stream; 2.86 inches in Oak Brook and 2.79 inches in Westmont.

events.event_narrative: Illinois Route 18 was under water just north of Illinois Route 17.  The viaduct on Illinois Route 23 south of Streator was flooded.  Dwight received 3.67 inches of rainfall.

Approximately six inches of running water was reported a mile east of Route 251 on North 2nd Road making the road impassable.  An observer near Seneca reported 5.17 inches of rain while an observer near Streator reported 4.76 inches of rainfall.

County emergency managers estimated that over 500 buildings were damaged by flooding across La Salle County.  In Marseilles, 1500 people were evacuated due to a compromised levee which led to dozens of homes and facilities being flooded along the river front.  Several barges broke loose from a tugboat on the Illinois River and rammed into the levee.  Five of the eight locks were damaged such that they could not close completely.  Flooding occurred in Utica east of Route 178 resulting in evacuations on the I&M Canal.  Creeks were reported out of their banks in Mendota.  A woman was killed on Route 351 as it passes over the Illinois River near Peru.  She drove around barricades and became stranded in knee-deep water.  Her body was found about two weeks later approximately 70 yards downstream.

The intersection of Route 47 and Plato Road was flooded.  Water was rushing over the road near Sandbloom Road and Bolz Road.  Standing water was reported on Route 72 and Randall Road.  Observers reported storm total rainfall of 5.34 inches near Algonquin and 4.36 inches near Elgin.

Flooding was occurring at a nursing home in Oregon.  Sandbags were sent to Stillman Valley. Creeks were rising out of their banks near Polo.  River Road was closed south of Route 72 near Byron. Also near Byron, the Rock River undercut portions of the shoulder of Route 2 in several spots.  Widespread standing water was reported county wide. An observer in Oregon reported a storm total of 5.00 inches or rainfall.

Widespread flooding was reported over much of DuPage County.  Dozens of homes were underwater in Towers of Four Lakes Village requiring emergency crews to rescue people trapped inside. Numerous roadways were covered with flowing water causing several cars to stall.  Lower levels of several apartment buildings were flooded.  Retention ponds were overflowing.  Roosevelt Road was closed between Wegner Drive and Joliet Street due to high water.  Portions of Route 53 were closed between 75th Street and Royce Road. Numerous basements were flooded near Elmhurst, Lisle, and Naperville. Some residents had to be rescued in Lisle. The Glen Ellyn Public Library building's sub-basement flooded under five feet of water and also received extensive damage on the first floor.  In Lombard, basements as well as first floors were flooded.  Approximately 30 streets in Lombard were completely submerged.||Du Page county received the most rainfall during this evening with several sites reporting over seven inches of rain.  Observers measured 7.34 inches near Naperville, 7.26 inches near Elmhurst, 7.12 inches near Aurora, and 7.01 inches near Lisle.

The hardest hit areas in Grundy County were Morris, Mazon, and Minooka.  Numerous rescues took place, including people trapped in vehicles in rising waters.  Forty-four patients at Morris Hospital were evacuated when the lower floor flooded.  The aqueduct that carries the I & M canal over Nettle Creek collapsed.  South of Morris, Pine Bluff Road was impassable with approximately a foot of water.
Numerous roads were closed across the county due to flooding.  An observer near Yorkville reported 6.30 inches of rain while another near Montgomery reported 5.66 inches.
Numerous roads were closed across the county due to flooding.  An observer in De Kalb reported 4.67 inches of rain. An observer in Shabbona reported 4.53 inches of rain.

A levee was breached in Lincolnshire requiring 49 homes to be evacuated.  Route 41 was closed between Route 137 and Route 176. Near Beach Park, water was reported over many roads, ponds were out of banks, and many homes had water up to doorsteps. County emergency managers estimated that 4,500 properties were affected by the flooding.

Witnesses described a tornado briefly touching down and hitting a barn, killing two horses, then lifting back up.  Six power poles were also blown down. Emergency managers found debris as far as approximately six miles away.

This is a continuation of a tornado that began in Tazewell County (NWS Central Illinois) and tracked across Woodford County, entering NWS Chicago county warning area in La Salle County, and finally ending in Livingston County.  The tornado entered La Salle County approximately half a mile east of State Route 251 north of Minonk where several power poles were snapped at the base along County Line Road.  On E 7th Road, a home had large portions of the roof removed.  Small outbuildings were completely destroyed.  More power poles were snapped on E 8th Road and again on N 2nd Road near the intersection of E 10th Road.  A machinery shed was completely destroyed on N 2nd Road about half a mile west of Dana.  On E 11th Road just north of Dana, an addition to a home was completely leveled with several outbuildings destroyed.  This tornado entered Livingston County just northeast of Dana around 11:41 AM CST.  Maximum wind speeds were estimated to be up to 135 mph.

This is a continuation of a tornado that began in Tazewell County (NWS Central Illinois) and tracked across Woodford County, entering NWS Chicago county warning area in La Salle County, and finally ending in Livingston County. The tornado entered Livingston County about a third of a mile north of E 2400 N Road where power poles were leaning.  Several outbuildings were heavily damaged or destroyed on E 2475 N Road.  Hardwood trees were snapped on N 200 E Road as well as wooden power poles.  A large shed housing a fire engine was completely destroyed with the fire engine rolled onto its side on Long Point Blacktop Road near the intersection of N 400 E Road.  On the northeast side of that intersection, a wooded area saw extensive tree damage with numerous trees sheared off about 20 to 30 feet from their bases.  The damage path ended about half a mile north of Long Point Blacktop Road between N 450 E Road and Route 23.  Maximum wind speeds were estimated to be up to 135 mph.

Video was received from a storm chaser showing a satellite tornado that formed just south of the long tracked tornado that moved across Livingston County.  This tornado only lasted a few minutes and appeared to stay over open fields with no damage evident.  Maximum wind speeds were estimated to be up to 75 mph.

The tornado formed just northwest of the intersection of E Braceville Road and S Carbon Hill Road where several softwood trees were uprooted.  The tornado moved northeast just north of E Reed Road where a single family residence sustained visible damage to its exterior while a metal outbuilding sustained roof and exterior wall damage.  A single family home sustained considerable damage near the intersection of Berta Road and Spring Road where two people were injured.  The tornado continued into a subdivision north of Spring Road where widespread minor damage occurred to several dozen homes.  Several homes received more substantial damage though, including partial loss of roofs and second story walls.  The tornado continued into Will County around 12:26 PM CST.  Maximum wind speeds were estimated to be up to 125 mph.

This is a continuation of a tornado that began at 12:22 PM CST in Grundy County. The tornado moved into  Will County on N Will Road just south of State Route 113.  There was considerable damage to businesses on State Route 113 between N Will Road and I-55.  An RV dealership had numerous vehicles overturned and damaged.  A two story structure lost its roof and had portions of its walls ripped off.  A model home was completely removed from its foundation on the north side of State Route 113.  A manufactured building had its roof ripped off with all the walls collapsed. Widespread tree damage was observed along the west side of I-55 where the tornado almost tracked parallel to as it weakened.  The tornado crossed I-55 near Widows Road where several hardwood trees were uprooted.  The tornado tracked into the Midewin Tallgrass Prairie where it damaged several metal structures just west of Route 53.  The tornado lifted just east of Route 53.  Maximum wind speeds were estimated to be up to 125 mph.

The tornado touched down south of W Bruns Road and east of S Kankakee Street.  This tornado quickly intensified to EF-2 damaging five houses along Bruns Road rendering them uninhabitable by removing large sections of the roofs and leading to partial wall collapse. Four high tension power line towers were bent along S Schoolhouse Road.  Two houses and a barn were heavily damaged on W Dralle Road where large portions of the roofs were ripped off.  Several trees were snapped and uprooted as well.  Another farm on S Scheer Road had roof damage consistent to EF-1 intensity.  The last sign of damage occurred just south of Steger Road where large branches were blown down.  Maximum winds were estimated to around 125 mph.

The tornado formed along the Kankakee-Will County Line just west of N 17480 E Road.  Large branches from hardwood trees were broken off while an older softwood tree was snapped at the base.  A hardwood tree was also snapped in half.  The tornado had estimated winds to around 100 mph.  The tornado continued into Will County at 1:01 PM CST.

This is a continuation of a tornado that formed in Kankakee County at 1:00 PM CST.  The tornado moved northeast into Will County just west of N 17480 E Road.  A large barn sustained significant damage to its roof and outer walls.  Two adjacent metal outbuildings also had partial roof loss.   Several softwood trees were snapped at the base or half way up with debris lofted about a thousand feet.  A 400 lb tractor blade was moved about 60 feet while a grain pipe that had been riveted to the silo was ripped away.  Minor tree damage was noted along E Delite Inn Road as well as minor damage to small barns and outbuildings.  The tornado had estimated winds to around 100 mph.

This is a continuation of a tornado that began in Champaign County (NWS Central Illinois) and tracked across Vermilion County before entering the NWS Chicago county warning area in southern Iroquois County. Three homes had minor damage to either outbuildings or large trees.
Four farms were impacted with several large trees down or snapped.  One outbuilding had its roof torn off.  Maximum winds were estimated to 80 mph.

The tornado touched down in Goodland causing several large grain bins to cave in on themselves with some of the surrounding scaffolding collapsing.  This portion of the storm was consistent with high-end EF-0 damage with estimated winds to 85 mph.  The tornado continued into Jasper County around 1:29 PM CST where it further intensified to EF-1.

This is a continuation of a tornado that touched down in Newton County at 1:27 PM CST.  The tornado mainly passed over open fields; however, near the end of the path an outbuilding was destroyed and small farm equipment moved, including one piece that was rolled into a grain storage bin.  Debris was noted as far as a mile downstream.  The highest winds were estimated to around 100 mph.

The tornado heavily damaged an outbuilding with several wood projectiles from the building stuck into a nearby garage roof. Debris from the outbuilding was lofted at least three miles downstream. Another outbuilding was heavily damaged and multiple trees were blown down or snapped. Maximum winds were estimated to be 95 mph. The tornado continued into White County (NWS Northern Indiana).

Multiple empty grain bins and outbuildings were destroyed across four farmsteads with large paths of debris thrown two miles downstream.  Utility poles were blown down along with dozens of trees that were snapped.  Maximum winds were estimated to 100 mph.
Freezing drizzle caused a glaze of ice to form on roads, leading to multiple cars sliding off the road into a ditch along Highway 173 near Machesney Park.
A third-story window near Michigan and Pearson shattered in the high winds.  No serious injuries were reported.

Significant flooding occurred in South Haven requiring at least 18 boat evacuations in the predawn hours and at least three homes were declared uninhabitable. events.event_narrative: Winds frequently gusted in excess of 48 knots for around 12 hours with a peak gust of 62.4 knots.  A 132-foot barge at Navy Pier broke loose from its mooring and was sunk after being battered by strong winds and large waves.
Strong winds uprooted 14 trees in Whiting Lakefront Park.
An elderly man died in his garage from hypothermia due to cold exposure.

Winds gusting 40 to 50 mph combined with light snow resulted in white out conditions along a portion of Interstate 55 near Gardner, IL. Between 17 and 22 cars were involved in a pile-up. Twelve people were taken to hospitals, including two people with serious to life threatening injuries. The interstate was shut down for around four hours.
An observer near Homewood measured 7.1 inches of snow by 7 AM with a storm total of 7.8 inches.
Winnebago ESDA reported white out conditions across the county with many vehicles stranded.
Boone County sheriff reported white out conditions across the county with many rural roads closed.
Lee County EM reported white out conditions across the county with many roads closed. State Route 52  was closed south of Dixon near the I-88 interchange due to stranded cars.
Whiteout conditions were reported along with numerous stranded vehicles.  Highway 52 was down to one lane due to severe drifting.
De Kalb County had to pull their plow fleet from the roads around 6 pm after the snow ended due to dangerous conditions.
There were a few stranded vehicles along with some drifting along and temporary whiteout conditions.

Emergency managers reported blowing and drifting in open areas along with stranded vehicles.  Temporary whiteout conditions were reported on sections of I-80 and I-55.
Emergency managers reported U.S. 34 was closed between Mendota and Earlville due to blowing snow and stranded vehicles.  Route 18 between U.S. 251 and Streator was also closed.

events.event_narrative: This is a continuation of a tornado that began in Winnebago County.  An emergency manager and trained spotters photographed a tornado that touched down south of Cherry Valley.  The tornado did not produce any damage. (Tornado 1b of 7).
A brief satellite tornado formed over far eastern Ogle County.  The tornado was confirmed during an aerial survey. (Tornado 3 of 7).

An emergency manager and trained spotters photographed a tornado that touched down south of Cherry Valley.  The tornado did not produce any damage.  The tornado continued into Boone County. (Tornado 1a of 7).

This tornado was identified from a storm chaser video and survey.  Heavy damage to two small outbuildings occurred on Paulson Road.  Maximum winds speeds were estimated to be 110 mph.  The tornado continued into Boone County. (Tornado 4a of 7).

This is a continuation of a tornado that began in Dekalb County.  This tornado was identified from a storm chaser video and survey.  Three barns were destroyed on Pearl Street Road.  Maximum winds speeds were estimated to be 110 mph. (Tornado 4b of 7).

This was a satellite tornado that formed from the same storm that formed the long tracked EF-4 tornado.  A small zoo was heavily damaged with walls collapsed on several outbuildings and small barns.  Three animals were killed.  Softwood trees 4 to 6 inches in diameter were snapped.  The estimated peak wind was 85 mph.  (Tornado 5 of 7).

Witnesses said the tornado touched down in a field then moved northeast destroying a detached garage.  The tornado ripped the roof off of a home though the walls mainly remained intact.  Several hardwood trees were snapped.  Maximum wind speeds were estimated to be 110 mph.  (Tornado 6 of 7).

A brief tornado snapped and uprooted 6 to 7 trees at a property on McGuire Road southeast of Harvard.  Minor tree damage occurred on the north side of the road before ending.  Maximum winds were estimated to 90 mph.  (Tornado 7 of 7).

This is the beginning of the Rochelle-Fairdale EF-4 tornado.  At its strongest, peak winds were estimated to be 200 mph.  The tornado touched down just northeast of Franklin Grove.  A large sheet metal building on IL-38 collapsed with failure of column anchorage.  Several smaller sheet metal buildings were destroyed along E Gurler Road. Peak winds in Lee County were estimated to 110 mph.  The tornado continued into Ogle County.  (Tornado 2a of 7).

This is the second segment of the Rochelle-Fairdale EF-4 tornado.  At its strongest, peak winds were estimated to be 200 mph which occurred during this segment of the storm.  The tornado entered Ogle County just west of IL-38 and moved northeast where it ripped the roof off of a small barn.  A neighborhood was hit on S Skare Court where damage was consistent with EF-3.  Some of the homes had large sections of the roofs ripped off while some less well constructed homes (nails instead of bolts) had collapsed walls.  The tornado continued northeast and intensified to EF-4 where several well constructed homes along South Richard Road and East Kuehl Court were completely destroyed with the slab swept clean.  Several outbuildings were destroyed along East Hemstock Road and South Center Road.  A residence on East Bethal Road received heavy damage with most of the outer walls collapsing.  The tornado once again intensified to EF-4  near IL-251 and IL-64 where well constructed homes were swept clean off their foundation.  A farmstead just northeast of the aforementioned intersection was also swept clean to the foundation.  A heavy barn was thrown and rolled on East Lindenwood Road.  In total, around 30 homes were damaged or destroyed around Rochelle.  The tornado continued into Dekalb County just north of East Quarry Road.  (Tornado 2b of 7).

This is the third segment of the Rochelle-Fairdale EF-4 tornado.  At its strongest, peak winds were estimated to be 200 mph.  The tornado entered the county just southwest of Fairdale before directly hitting the small community.  Peak winds were estimated at 165 mph in Dekalb County, rating this section of the tornado a high end EF-3.  Approximately 71 homes in the community had been damaged, 17 of which had been completely destroyed with all walls collapsed or removed from the buildings.  Some homes that were only nailed to the foundation were swept clean.  Two fatalities and 11 injuries occurred in Fairdale.  A 67-year-old woman and her neighbor, a 69-year-old woman, were both killed in their homes.  The tornado began to shift north (left) at this point during its lifecycle as it left Fairdale.  Several homes were heavily damaged with large sections of the roofs removed along Wheeler road and dozens of trees were snapped and uprooted.  A few trees were debarked.  The second story was ripped off of a home near the intersection of McNeal Road and Irene Road.  A two-story rebar reinforced cinder block silo was destroyed.  The tornado continued into Boone County just east of Irene Road.  (Tornado 2c of 7).

This is the fourth segment of the Rochelle-Fairdale EF-4 tornado.  At its strongest, peak winds were estimated to be 200 mph.  The tornado entered Boone County just east of Irene Road.  No damage occurred and the tornado lifted shortly after entering the county.  (Tornado 2d of 7).

The tornado touched down approximately 1.4 miles east of Symerton snapping large tree limbs west of Warner Bridge Road.  The tornado moved east and downed trees and a power pole along Peotone-Wilmington Road just west of Gougar Road.  The tornado turned southeast and impacted a Kennel and an adjacent residence where EF-1 damage was noted due to roof and tree damage.  This included multiple snapped or uprooted trees.   The tornado moved toward Tully Road and flipped multiple 320 lb grain bins over a garage and into a field across Tully Road.  Damage was noted to metal outbuildings.  The tornado continued southeast and impacted two farmsteads near Kennedy and Cedar Roads  where EF-1 damage occurred to trees and a machine shed.  Metal siding and additional debris from the shed was thrown a half mile downstream where the tornado dissipated in a field.

Several trees fell onto recreational vehicles and it was estimated that around 100 of the 300 homes in the area received some degree of damage.  One person was taken to the hospital in serious condition, and six others were injured.  Peak winds were estimated to be 130 mph. (Tornado 3 of 10).

A tornado crossed through the center of Mendota resulting in significant tree damage.  Some trees were blown down onto structures and at least one fell onto a vehicle.  The tornado touched down near the intersection of Knoll Crest Drive and S Park Avenue where numerous hardwood trees were snapped.  One to three inch branches were broken as the tornado crossed 13th Avenue. A large trunk was split on Washington Street.  Trees were uprooted on 5th Street near 5th Avenue. (Tornado 6b of 10).
The tornado blew off a portion of the roof of a house and snapped a large tree.  Peak winds were estimated at 95 mph. (Tornado 7 of 10).

The tornado touched down near Higgins Road and Dupont Road where softwood trees were snapped. The tornado moved east-southeast where trees and power poles were snapped along N Gorman Road.  The most significant damage was noted as the tornado crossed S Carbon Hill Road just south of Division Street, entering Coal City. Dozens of homes were heavily damaged in Coal City with three completely destroyed.  Two of these homes were well built and had at least part of their structure bolted down to the foundation with bolts secured by nuts.  Two high tension metal trusses were downed including one that was crumpled along Hunters Run.  Hundreds of trees were snapped or uprooted.  Numerous utility poles were downed.  Peak winds were estimated to be 160 mph with a max width of three quarters of a mile.  The tornado continued into Will County.  (Tornado 8a of 10).

In Elk Grove Village, a  canopy was blown off a gas station on Higgins Rd between Elmhurst Rd and Touhy Ave. Also, a roof was blown off an industrial building at 2300 Higgins Rd. Also, there was a overturned tractor trailer on I-39 southbound just south of the I-80 and I-39 interchange, which is 2 miles northeast of LaSalle, IL.  This occurred around 400 pm CST.

Snow began in Newton County around 515 am CST.  However, blizzard impacts were felt around 415 pm CST.  At 800 pm CST, near blizzard conditions were seen in Mount Ayr, based on impacts of heavy snow and concurrent blowing snow with near zero visibility reported. State of emergency had been declared for Newton County. Numerous motorists were stranded and needed rescue. There were also many power outages across the county. The highest snow report was 8.0 inches 7 miles SE of Lake Village.

Snow began around 600 am CST in Porter county.  However, blizzard conditions didn't begin until after 200 pm CST.  At 810 pm CST in Valparaiso, IN, near blizzard conditions continued with visibility between one quarter mile and zero. Snow drifts were around 2 feet. At 900 pm, near blizzard conditions were reported based on heavy snow and concurrent blowing snow with zero visibility reported. The ramp to southbound I-65 was closed by State Police for a time due to stranded drivers, their cars and trucks stuck in the snow. State of emergency was declared for Porter County around 530 pm CST. Numerous motorists were stranded and needed rescue. Some of the highest snow totals were 15.0 inches reported 2 miles north northeast of Lakes of the Four Seasons, and 13.0 inches 6 miles WSW of Valparaiso.

At Gary Airport at 345 pm CST, winds at the AWOS gusted to 62 mph. At 800 pm CST, heavy snow and blowing snow reduced visibility to near zero. State of Emergency was declared for Lake County. Numerous motorists were stranded and needed rescue. There were also numerous power outages across the county. Some of the highest snowfall totals were 15.5 inches 1 mile NNW of Hobart, 14.5 inches 2 miles WSW of Crown Point, and 13.3 inches in Lowell.

At 800 pm CST, near zero visibility was reported due to heavy snow and blowing snow. Many motorists were stranded during the afternoon into the early evening. Highest snowfall totals were 10.5 inches around 2 miles SSW of Rensselaer, and 10.0 inches 1 mile north northwest of DeMotte.
